articleTitle: Passivity-Based Active Disturbance Rejection Control for Position/Force Control of a Holonomic-Constrained Mobile Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, a passivity-based active disturbance rejection control scheme is presented for an omnidirectional mobile manipulator for position/force control under dynamic uncertainties and external disturbances. A detailed dynamic model of the omnidirectional mobile manipulator and the passive mechanical properties of it are systematically analyzed. The presented scheme of this paper is comprised of a passivity-based controller and an extended state observer. The extended state observer estimates dynamic uncertainties and external disturbances of the control system. Then the passivity-based controller compensates them actively. The stability of the proposed control system and the convergence of the observation error are analyzed. Simulation results certify the excellent robustness and the validity of the presented control system.

articleTitle: An Improved Back Propagation Neural Network Forecasting Model Using Variation Fireworks Algorithm for Short-time Traffic Flow
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Short-term traffic flow has complicated non-linear characteristic, and it has a similar seasonality. This paper presents an improved Back Propagation neural network for Short-time traffic flow prediction using Variation Fireworks Algorithm. In the new model, we use self-adaption explosion amplitude to resolve the contradiction between local search and global search while maintaining the good properties of better fireworks. Furthermore, this model, using self-variation mutation operator, can improve the features of better fireworks. For increasing the diversity, we introduce random mapping out-of-boundary sparks instead of modulo operator. It is applied to real-world data collected from the Second Ring Road of Beijing, China and is compared with three traffic prediction models. The consequences show that the new model has higher accuracy and can be served as forecasting of short-term traffic flow. And the model shows better result than the Back Propagation (BP) neural network model, Particle Swarm optimization Back Propagation (PSO-BP) neural network and Fireworks Algorithm Back Propagation (FWA-BP) neural network model.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a New Type of Spatial Flexible Micromanipulation Platform
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: A novel type of spatial flexible micromanipulator is designed based on flexure hinges, which can realize the translational motion along the Z axis and rotations around X and Y axes. During the design, we use the bridge displacement amplifier as translational pairs to drive platform movement, with a flexure hinges instead of the traditional hinges. The magnification ratio of the bridge displacement amplifier is calculated by the method of the elastic analysis with consideration of rotational and translational stiffness. The simulation and analysis are carried out with ANSYS Workbench. The theoretical calculation and simulation error are 8.77%. The micro-operation platform is analyzed by static simulation and modal analysis. The results show that the micromanipulator has a large working space and strong anti - interference ability, with a fast dynamic response speed.

articleTitle: Silicon Prediction Model of Blast Furnace Based on ARX and PCR
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Silicon content in hot metal ([Si]) is an important variable in actual blast furnace production, since it is regarded as the chief indicator of in-furnace thermal status(IFTS). For actual applications, practical [Si] prediction models need to predict the long-term outcome. In other words, if the lead time is shorter, it is easier to predict [Si] correctly, but it is too late to take actions. This paper presents a long-term prediction model. In order to predict the long-term outcome, the delay times of the input variables are analyzed, and a prediction model based on auto-regressive eXogenous(ARX) model is established where Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) is used to find the optimal model from a set of the alternative models. Principal component regression(PCR) is used to compute future [Si] for reducing dimension and noise filtration. The [Si] prediction model is very helpful for BF operation because it predict the long-term outcome. It can assist BF operators to monitor and control the IFTS timely. The practical application results show the effectiveness of the model.

articleTitle: Coverage control for heterogeneous mobile sensor networks on a circle with guaranteed collision avoidance
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper studies the coverage control problem for a mobile sensor network on a unit circle and the sensors have different maximum velocities. We model each sensor as a disk to approximately describe the actual size of sensors. The coverage goal is to minimize the largest arrival time from the mobile sensor network to any point on the circle and the sensors should avoid collision with each other throughout the coverage task. Then, a distributed control law with input constraint is developed to guarantee that the sensors can arrive to the optimal locations without collisions. Therefore, the coverage goal can achieve safely. Finally, a numerical simulation is presented to show the effectiveness of our distributed control law.

articleTitle: Research on Adaptive Monte Carlo Location Algorithm Aided by Ultra-Wideband Array
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of poor initial location performance, global location failure and kidnap problems of Adaptive Monte Carlo Location (AMCL) algorithm, this paper proposes the algorithm based on ultra-wideband (UWB) array to calculate the pose of mobile robot and the AMCL algorithm assisted by the UWB array. The relative position of the UWB tag on mobile robot is solved to calculate the absolute pose of the mobile robot. The absolute pose is integrated into the AMCL algorithm to assist mobile robot in initial location. At the same time, it is used as a reference pose to detect whether mobile robot has located globally and kidnap or not, and develop recovery strategy of global location failure or kidnap for relocating successfully. Finally, under the gazebo simulation platform, the simulation experiment is carried out. The results show that the algorithm for solving pose based on the UWB array can solve the pose of mobile robot accurately, the rapidity and stability of the initial location are improved, global location failure or kidnap can be detected, and mobile robot can recover to locate successfully in the case of location failure or kidnap.

articleTitle: Research of Camera Calibration Method Based on Confocal Conic Curve
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, a camera calibration method based on improved ellipse fitting is proposed. First, Hough Transform and the Least Squares are used to fit ellipse of calibration graph. Then, by means of the invariance of the eigenvalue of the confocal curve projection mapping, the homography matrix is obtained in the form of cubic projection. And the generalized eigenvalue decomposition is carried out to get the internal parameters of the camera. Compared with the traditional chess method, the calibration method proposed in this paper does not need to extract feature points and has a faster calibration speed and guaranteed the accuracy of calibration results.

articleTitle: Estimation of Oxygen Concentration for Roller Kiln Based on Boundary Measurements
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper investigates the estimation of oxygen concentration for the roller kiln based on boundary measurements. Firstly, we establish the oxygen transportation model based on the principle of mass conservation. Secondly, we optimize the parameters of the proposed model by the least square method and particle swarm optimization (PSO). Then, we adopt the finite difference method based on second order central difference scheme to simulate the steady-state distribution. The resulting distribution is applied to estimate the internal furnace oxygen concentration. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by comparing the estimated concentration with the real sample data in terms of the root mean square error (RMSE) and the maximum average absolute error (MAE).

articleTitle: Data-driven Fault Diagnosis Scheme for Complex Integrated Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: From 13th national five-year to 15th five-year development period, the new generation of scientific facilities is under construction in China. Control systems are critical for the safety operation of novel scientific facilities. The traditional fault diagnosis technology based on analytical models is not applicable to complex process. In the paper, the data-driven fault diagnosis scheme under three complex conditions including nonlinear controlled process, non-Gaussian noise and incomplete information is analyzed in depth. Finally, the components and elements of simulation verification environment are given.

articleTitle: Improved object segmentation technique in digital fringe projection
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Object segmentation from invalid points such as shadows and background is a key factor in digital fringe projection 3D shape measurement. Conventional methods for object segmentation based on modulation level normally work well in dark background, however, they lose accuracy with a variety of backgrounds. In this paper, we proposed two coding images and applied them in an improved framework for object segmentation. The shadows are detected from modulation histogram, and the background is detected from intensity histogram of the coding images. Experiments are designed on different background conditions for analyzing and verifying the segmentation performance of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: The Current Balance Realization of Dual-Redundancy PMSM based on the Sliding Mode Error Compensation
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The current imbalance phenomenon of two sets of three-phase symmetric coils may occur during the operation of the Dual-Redundancy permanent magnet synchronous motor and the harm caused by unbalanced current are analyzed. Then the mathematic model of the Dual-Redundancy permanent magnet synchronous motor is established. Finally, a new current balance strategy based on sliding mode error compensation is proposed. With the coordinate transformation of the sampling currents, the difference between the q-axis current of two sets of windings is used for the input of the sliding mode error controller. The outputs of the sliding mode error controller and the PI controller are superimposed to be the input signal of SVPWM. As the simulation and experimental results shown, the new current balance strategy based on sliding mode error compensation has a good dynamic response, which can realize the current balance of two sets of three-phase symmetric coils quickly and effectively. The current balance strategy is also suitable for the current balance of other Dual-Redundancy electromagnetic mechanisms.

articleTitle: Automatic Detection of Linear Mesoscale Convective Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The Linear Mesoscale Convective System (MCS) is a vital weather system that causes severe weather such as heavy rain, hail, thunderstorms, and tornadoes. The traditional manual operation cannot give an effective means for timely observation and forecasting of weather systems due to the increase number in meteorological data. Thus, this paper presents an automatic approach for identifying linear MCSs from radar reflectivity data using support vector machine (SVM). First, a multi-scale segmentation method is used to segment a linear MCS from radar reflectivity images. Then, the linear MCS is standardized to an 8×8 region, and a 64D feature is used to describe the linear MCS. Finally, the detection of linear MCSs is performed by SVM. It is shown in this paper that the linear MCSs can be well automatically identified, and the automatic recognition results are potentially useful for accurate nowcasting.

articleTitle: Facial Expression recognition via neurons partially activated discriminated ELM
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Facial expression recognition is a very meaningful and challenging research topic and it has been widely used in many problems in the artificial intelligence era. Such as human computer interaction, intelligent family robot, patient intelligence diagnosis, and driver safety. In this paper, we proposed a new approach for facial recognition based on ELM(Extreme Learning Machine). Traditional ELM is famous for it simple structure and high accuracy both in classification and regression problems. However, the number of neurons is hard to determine in a given problem. The core idea is force the l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>,1-norm on the weight matrix of hidden layer to select the activated neurons, thus to obtain a simple network structure. Then, we add the migration factor into loss term to enlarge the distance of different types of facial expressions. Compared to state-of-the-art method at present, our method is competitive in accuracy and robustness. The experiments of facial expression recognition are carried out on JAFFE facial expression database and getting excellent performance.

articleTitle: Detection Method of Series Arc Fault Based on Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Arcing fault is an important factor of electrical fire, which cause it very hard to be detected by the traditional protection appliances, as a result, a new method is urgent needed to detect arcing fault accurately. At present, methods of detecting arcing fault is based on Fourier transform have disadvantages such as high rate of misjudgment and limited range of load. In this paper, we purposed a new method that based on db3 wavelet decomposition to detect arcing fault. By analyzing the changing rate of current energy in normal and fault conditions, using db3 wavelet to analysis its current characteristic of frequency band energy, we can extract approximation signals a5 and detail signal d1~d5. By comparing the energy ratio during each frequency band, we can determine whether the arcing fault occurred or not. Both the theoretical and experimental results show that the method has good reliability and correctness of fault arc detection.

articleTitle: A Reliability-based Design optimization of Crane Metallic Structure based on Ant colony optimization and LHS
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Design optimization for crane metal structures (CMSs) is of great significance to reducing the weight and cost of structure. Although uncertainty is an inherent property existing in structure and deterministic design optimization (DDO) may result in an unreliable structure, optimization design considering uncertainty factors in crane structure is rare in studies at present. In view of this, the reliability-based design optimization (RBDO) is employed to the design of CMSs with random design variables and parameters in our research work. A discrete double loop RBDO model was constructed. In the inner loop, Latin hypercube sampling (LHS) combining with Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) were used to analyze the reliability of every design point of every constraint. In the outer loop, the ant colony optimization (ACO) algorithm was utilized to obtain the optimal result satisfying deterministic and probabilistic constraints. The engineering case shows that compared with the DDO, the RBDO can achieve a better tradeoff between cost and reliability based on security requirements.

articleTitle: Image Fusion Based Local Graph Matching for Plant Cell Tracking
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Developing robust tracking algorithms for four-dimensional (3D + time) plant cells and their division is extremely important for obtaining spatiotemporal measurements of cell behavior patterns. The tracking of plant cells across noisy microscopy image sequences is very challenging, because plant cells in noisy region cannot be correctly segmented and cause serious errors in subsequent cell tracking procedure. This paper proposed an image fusion based local graph matching method to track plant cells. First, the nonsubsampled contourlet transform sparse representation (NSCTSR) image fusion method is used to fusing a confocal plant cell image stack into a single image, which has the higher contrast of image quality and richer information than any single image in the image stack. Second, the local graph matching approach is used to track the plant cells in the fused images, by exploiting the cells' local graph structure and contextual information. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can improve the quality of the cell image, and reach a higher tracking accuracy for plant cells than the previous method.

articleTitle: Multiscale Complex Network for Analyzing the Wind Field from Different Heights and Seasons
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The multiscale phenomena is widely encountered in many nonlinear systems. Uncovering the dynamic characteristics of wind signals is a challenging problem with significant engineering applications. In order to solve this problem, we infer multiscale complex networks from wind speed signals in different seasons and heights. Specifically, we obtain a set of wind speed time series with different time scales using the coarse graining technique and then map those time series into multiscale complex networks using phase space reconstruction technique. Furthermore, we introduce three measures, i.e., clustering coefficient entropy (CCE), mean values of CCE with large scales, variances of CCE, to quantitatively analyze the dynamic and seasonal characteristics of wind signals. The results suggest that the CCE and its derivative index can accurately reflect the dynamic and seasonal changes of wind speed signals. The combination of complex network analysis and multiscale analysis provides an effective method for the detection of wind field behavior.

articleTitle: Consensus Dynamics With Application to Vision-based Localization
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, a class of new consensus dynamics over undirected graph is proposed. The condition of persistence of excitation is imposed on the coupling matrices to reach consensus. Then based on the proposed consensus algorithms, an adaptive localization algorithm using primarily onboard visual sensing is developed for autonomous robots in GPS- denied environments. The convergence of the proposed localization algorithm is interpreted in the framework of consensus. Finally, some numerical studies are presented to validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Fitting the Variations from the Wind Speed to the Active Power of a Wind Powered Generator by a Low-Pass Filter
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: A smart electrical grid must accommodate all kinds of green renewable energy, especially the wind power. The mapping from a wind speed to the active power of a mechanical wind powered generator is a key fundamental technique for the wind power accommodation. To find explicit analytical functions from a wind speed to the active power, according to the law of rotation of a rigid body in rotational motion in physics, the function from wind speed variations to active power variations can be approximately reduced to a first-order low-pass filter. This analytical function is verified by three time series, i.e., the wind speed, blade rotation and active power with 10s sampling period. The variational components of wind speed and active power are decomposed by the 7 points smoothing filter, a linear Gaussian filtering and the biorthogonal 6.8 wavelet (bior6.8). The standard deviations ratio of active power variations to wind speed variations is very close to the magnitude frequency response of a first-order low-pass filter. The cross wavelet transform and wavelet coherence between time series of wind speed and active power also confirm the filter function. The numerical simulations show that a first-order low-pass filter can approximately represent the function from wind speed variations to active power variations.

articleTitle: Railway Optimal Slip Ratio Control Using Extremum Seeking Algorithm With Adaptive Amplitude Tuning
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The key technology of anti-slip control system is to identify the optimal slip ratio in individual conditions for railway applications. In this paper, an extended state observer (ESO) is proposed for the immeasurable varying adhesion coefficient. With the estimated modeling error information, the deviation is eliminated by the designed compensation control rate, which results in an accurate adhesion coefficient observation. Then an extremum seeking (ES) algorithm with adaptively tuned amplitude is proposed to calculate the optimal slip ratio under current road conditions. Compared with classical ES-based methods, the proposed method has smaller oscillations and better dynamic performance. In order to get the maximum braking force, the feedback linearization control framework is proposed for a nonlinear controller of wheel optimal slip ratio. To increase the stability and robustness of the control system, a Lyapunov function with integral form is constructed. The simulation result demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: An Improved Image Thresholding Method Based On Two-Dimensional Histogram
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The traditional two-dimensional histogram thresholding method ignores the existence of noise, which may lead to misclassification problem. Moreover, the calculation of the optimal threshold by two-dimensional Renyi entropy is too complex. To avoid these drawbacks, an improved segmentation method which combining grayscale-gradient histogram and traditional two-dimensional histogram is proposed in this paper. First, the gray-gradient histogram is constructed by using the gray value of each pixel and the gray value of its neighborhood. The noise points can be removed according to the distance between the pixels and the horizontal axis in grayscale-gradient histogram. After de-noising, the pixels are located near the main diagonal in the traditional two-dimensional histogram. Then, the distance from each pixel to the origin can be used to select the optimal segmentation threshold, which reduces the computational complexity from $O(L^{4})$ to $O(L^{2})$. The experimental result shows that the improved method proposed in this paper is faster, more accurate and more robust than traditional two-dimensional method, thus especially suitable for low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) images.

articleTitle: Epileptic Seizure Detection using DWT Based Weighted Visibility Graph
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Epilepsy is a common neurological disorder of the brain and can be assessed by electroencephalogram (EEG). By combining discrete wavelet transformation (DWT) and weighted visibility graph (WVG), we employed a new approach for detecting epileptic seizure from EEG. First, DWT is applied to decompose EEG into different frequency bands, then WVG is constructed from the sub-band signals. Average weighted degree and clustering coefficient are extracted to characterize the topological structure of the networks and distinguish different brain states (healthy, inter-ictal and ictal). Four different test cases are designed to evaluate the performance of our DWT-WVG method. The obtained results demonstrate that both features are effective to discriminate the ictal EEG from interictal EEG or EEG recorded from healthy subjects.

articleTitle: User Selection with Energy Efficiency for Cooperative Spectrum Sensing in Energy Harvesting Cognitive Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, we consider a RF energy harvesting cognitive radio network (CRN) in which cooperating secondary users (SUs) are equipped with energy harvesting capabilities. The SUs can harvest energy by converting the received radio frequency (RF) signal into electricity. It is assumed that the SUs have different SNRs due to their distances from the primary user (PU). Our objective is to maximize the energy efficiency of the CRN subject to the sensing accuracy constraint and energy constraint by finding the optimal SUs to participate in the cooperative spectrum sensing. The problem is solved analytically based on the convex optimization framework. After acquiring the optimal conditions based on karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT)conditions, an iterative algorithm is proposed to find the SUs for spectrum sensing. Since the problem is a NP-complete problem, we simplify it through mapping discrete parameter into real domain. Therefore, we can decide which SUs are selected for spectrum sensing at a lower computational complexity. A priority-based SU selection algorithm in cooperative spectrum sensing is proposed to improve the energy efficiency. Simulation results show that the proposed approach can improve the energy efficiency.

articleTitle: A Point-match-based Distance-perception Approach for UAV Autonomous Transmission-line Inspection
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper aims to resolve the problem of safety distance perception during UAV autonomous inspection along one side of overhead transmission lines. To this end, we design a complex but effective scheme to address projective distortion, viewpoint change and cloud interference. First, we compute the vanishing point of transmission lines and utilize it to filter the detected transmission lines, which effectively reduces the interference of cloud and illumination. Next, we rectify original image and maximize the recovery of parallel property between transmission lines by initializing and optimizing homography matrix. Thereafter, an adaptive grouping algorithm is adopted before the final line segment interval statistic to make distance perception algorithm more reliable. Finally, we test the whole scheme in a practical field environment and get an satisfying result.

articleTitle: Cooperative 4D Guidance for Multiple UAVs Based on Tensor Field
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper presents a four dimensional (4D) vector field guidance (VFG) method multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in time-constrained cooperative flight tasks. To guide a UAV approaching the desired position exactly at the certain arrival time, a time-synchronized VFG algorithm named tensor field is adopted. With the help of tensor field, a comprehensive 4D guidance method is designed for the cooperation of multiple UAVs. The conflicts between UAVs and obstacles are detected by Protected Airspace Zone, and the Physicomimetic algorithm is applied to make conflict resolution. To get optimal guidance performance, the tuning parameters of tensor filed are optimized by sequential quadratic programming. The proposed method is verified by a dynamic simulation where multiple UAVs cooperatively complete a challenging simultaneous arrival flight task.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Information Acquisition System Based on New Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In order to boost the data acquisition efficiency in the practical application, realizes video surveillance via wireless sensor network, this paper presents an information acquisition system based on new wireless sensor network, designing and implementing an integration of two networks which are ZigBee and Wi-Fi. It exploits each advantage of different networks focusing on information acquisition and transmission under particular working environment, breaks through the limitation of single wireless communication both in function and performance, and adopts mobile terminal as the control mode. This paper elaborates how to collect information on temperature, humidity and smoke concentration via ZigBee network and transmit video signal via Wi-Fi network. Data from multi-terminal nodes are aggregated and uploaded to the intelligent gateway including coordinator, and the webcam built in gateway is used to collect video information which is transmitted to terminal devices. A custom designed Android graphical user interface (GUI) application is also developed to enable automated and manual control of the system and users will capture the real time situation through Android GUI application.

articleTitle: A finger-vein extraction algorithm based on local Radon transform
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Finger-vein recognition, as a emerging biometric technology, has attracted considerable attention in the biometric authentication field because of its unique advantages. The primary task of finger-vein recognition is extracting vein patterns from an infrared finger-vein image. However, due to the light conditions and tissue structure of fingers, the captured image contains vein patterns as well as the noise and irregular shading which can seriously weaken the capability of a finger-vein recognition system in practical application. To settle this problem, in this study, we propose a robust vein pattern extraction method based on local Radon transform. Firstly, given a pixel, we calculate the values along six directions in the neighborhood of the pixel using local Radon transform. Secondly, on basis of the values along six directions, the primary vein orientation and its normal vector can be determined. Thirdly, to further reduce the impact of noise, we compute the curvature along the normal vector and verify whether the pixel belongs to vein patterns by certain rules. Finally, a local binarization method is employed for extracting vein patterns and matched by the template method. The Experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach are robust and reliable for improving the performance of the finger-vein identification system.

articleTitle: Automatic Cutting Control of Deformable Objects with Vision/Force Feedback
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The study of deformable object cutting operation is at a preliminary stage. This is due to the high-dimensional deformation and time-varying topology caused by the interaction between the object and the cutting tool. This paper proposed a cutting control method based on vision and force feedback so that the tool can cut along a pre-designed trajectory automatically. Using the improved Finite Element Method (FEM), we can model the deformable object offline and update the model in real time. At the same time, the physical parameters are estimated online with visual feedback on the surface to improve the robustness of modeling errors. Through force feedback, the resistance of the cutting tool can be reduced by adopting the pressing and slicing approach, thus a precise cutting with a smaller deformation can be achieved. The proposed approach is validated by cutting soft foam experimentally.

articleTitle: Fixed-time Formation Control for First-order Multi-agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, the fixed-time formation control is studied for multi-agent systems with first-integrator dynamics. Using the neighboring state information, the fixed-time formation protocols are designed for both time-invariant and time-varying formation cases. Then for the two cases, it can be demonstrated that the multi-agent systems can realize the expected formation within the prescribed settling time that is independent of initial conditions. To make the system move as a whole after realizing the expected formation, a reference speed input is added into the distributed protocols. Simulations are included to demonstrate the correctness of our theoretical results.

articleTitle: Hardware Implementation of the Cerebellar Neural Network with Conductance-based Models
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Cerebellar cortex plays a vital role in motor learning. To investigate the functions of the cerebellar cortex, a hardware model simulating the cerebellar cortex is implemented on a FPGA chip with the dynamics of the functional cerebellum. The conductance-based models are used to realize the functions of the cerebellar cells and three types of synaptic current models are used to realize the interactions among these cells. The cerebellar models implemented on FPGA can respond the stimulus in 0.02ms, which makes the hardware model more flexible. The hardware model simulates different firing rates of Purkinje cells with different afferent stimulus, so that the action potential maps of five types of cerebellar cells are obtained on the oscilloscope. The results of the hardware implementation are consistent with the biological dynamics of the mammalian cerebellar, which means the functional cerebellum model is reliable and feasible.

articleTitle: The Effect of Sensor Position Uncertainties in Passive Target Tracking
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: We investigate the effect of sensor position uncertainties in passive target tracking in this paper, using the noisy time difference of arrival measurements. The sensor position uncertainty is considered to be a random noise in the TDOA measurement model. Because the TDOA measurement function is nonlinear to the unknown true sensor positions, we develop an augmented cubature Kalman filter method to deal with it. In comparison with the classical standard cubature Kalman filtering method, the proposed method suffers from higher computational complexity, however, its tracking performance is considerably improved. The performance of the proposed approach is verified through numerical Monte Carlo simulations.

articleTitle: Research on improved model predictive control Strategy based on MLD model
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Aiming at the three-phase inverter, an improved model predictive control strategy based on mixed logical dynamical(MLD) model is proposed. Firstly, the state equation of the three-phase inverter with the switching function is established. By including the logic variable to judge the switching state of each subinterval and its constraints and the conditional changes of the circuit, a three-phase inverter MLD model is built. Then, an improved model predictive control strategy based on convex optimization algorithm is come up with according to the model. The control strategy can effectively reduce the harmonic content of the output current and the dynamic adjustment time of the system, and the algorithm computation time is greatly shortened.

articleTitle: Transient Eddy Current Loss and Magnetic Field Distribution of Single-phase Three-legged Transformer under DC Bias
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In order to calculate eddy current loss and magnetic field distribution in iron core of single-phase three-legged transformer under DC bias, and to analyze local overheating problem, this paper puts forward to the coupling model of transient electric circuit and magnetic circuit considering core topology and nonlinearity of ferromagnetic materials. The transient distribution and variation of eddy current loss and magnetic field of single-phase three-Iegged transformer under different bias conditions are studied. The result shows that the waveform of transient eddy current loss and magnetic field in the iron core are shifted under DC bias. The amplitude of the eddy current loss and magnetic field grow nonlinearly with DC. The amplitude in B phase core column grows faster, which indicates the DC intrusion has greater influence on B phase core column.

articleTitle: A Novel Hand-eye Calibration Method of a Robot-Laser Scanner System for Large-scale Metrology
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: High-flexibility and high-precision are required in large-scale measurement for advanced manufacture. A robot-laser scanner system, which inherits the good flexibility of industrial robot and high accuracy of laser scanner, is a research focus recently. To obtain high measurement accuracy, hand-eye calibration is essential for this system. A novel two-step method, including primary calibration and optimization calibration, is proposed to calibrate the hand-eye of the measurement system. The primary calibration method is based on laser tracker and a well-designed tetrahedron, which can avoid the effect resulted from the parameter errors of industrial robot. Additionally, an optimizing calibration method by transforming the hand-eye calibration result into SE (3) is proposed to calculated the mean value of multiple primary calibration results, aiming to improve the calibration accuracy. Finally, a comparative experiment is conducted to verify the feasibility and accuracy of optimizing calibration method. It was found that comparing to the typical hand-eye calibration method, the optimizing method improves the mean repeat measurement accuracy by 23.4%, and the absolute measurement accuracy is also improved, with max/mean accuracy of 0.222 mm/0.178 mm.

articleTitle: Time Series Denoising Based on Empirical Mode Decomposition and Dictionary Learning
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Time series denoising is an inevitable problem in many processes of time series analysis and forecasting. In this paper, a novel denoising method based on empirical mode decomposition (EMD) and dictionary learning is proposed. With the method of EMD, the original signals are adaptively decomposed into a finite number of intrinsic mode functions (IMF). Then we apply the wavelet thresholding method to distinguish the noise components and effective components of the original signals for subsequent dictionary learning. Next, the K-SVD dictionary training algorithm is used to learn inner structures and properties of effective compositions and noise respectively. Finally, the noise of time series can be removed using this combined method of EMD and dictionary learning. To demonstrate the effect of combination strategy, we compare the performance of our proposed method to two state-of-the-art algorithms, i.e., wavelet thresholding algorithm (WTA) and EMD thresholding algorithm (EMD-TA) with two commonly used evaluating metrics: signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and correlation coefficient (CC). The results show that the proposed denoising method provides a competitive performance to the traditional denoising techniques.

articleTitle: Popularity Prediction of News Event Based on ELM and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: With the popularization of the Internet, the impact of news events on the society is growing. Research on the evolution of news event popularity could help netizens to grasp the overall development of news events. At present, the timeliness of the popularity prediction method for news event is prevalently weak and the data set is insufficient. This paper captures the real-time data from Baidu news search engine, and builds the predictive model of news event popularity based on ELM (Extreme Learning Machine). According to the similarity between news events and the prediction error of news event popularity, we propose the ELM-based prediction method by introducing the transfer learning strategy which considers the normalization of peak values of the popularity series. Our method is beneficial for establishing the prediction model under the non-independent distribution with missing data in the modeling process. The experimental results show that our method can predict the popularity of news event timely and effectively.

articleTitle: Automated cell manipulation through 3D bio-scaffold via dielectrophoresis
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a scaffold which could be used for cell manipulation via dielectrophoresis (DEP). The base of the scaffold was fabricated with a biodegradable polymer, polylactic acid (PLA) by a 3D printer. The fabricated structure was then coated with a thin layer of conductive material, in order to be served as electrodes for DEP manipulation. The designed structure was determined after the electric field simulation by the finite element analysis software COMSOL. MC3T3 cells were seeded onto the PLA and gold coated PLA (G-PLA), in order to investigate the influence of the conductive layer on the attaching and culturing of cells. The fabricated structure was then served as the electrodes for patterning cells via DEP mechanism. Cellular patterns were formed along the side and the corner of the scaffold. The patterned cells were further cultured for a week and could cover the surface of the scaffold. As the experiment results shows, this new scaffold could be used for 3D cell seeding and patterning for the development of bone tissue engineering.

articleTitle: An Improved Noise Filtering Approach for Multi-frequency Phase Sensitive Demodulation
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: As a key role in multi-frequency signal processing, multi-frequency phase sensitive demodulation (PSD) can be used in communication, sonar, bio-impedance measurement, mutual induction based non-destructive test,etc. Actually, the PSD is a matched filter to the reference signal; and in the presence of Gaussian noise, it can also be regarded as an optimal linear filter. However, in a practical measurement system, the noise often possesses impulsive characteristics,i.e. impulsive noise. Thus, how to effectively reduce the impulsive noise is a challenging research task. This paper introduces a method for the impulsive noise reduction in multi-frequency PSD. It takes full advantage of the signal period and the well-known de-noising features of the median filter (MF). Both simulation and experiment validate the proposed method in reducing the effects of impulsive noise for multi-frequency PSD. The results also demonstrated that the proposed method can achieve higher SNR and better robust.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic MPPT Control Based on Improved KMTOA in Complex Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Under the complicated environment, the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) ofPV system is carried out by traditional algorithm, which is very easy to be failed due to tracking to local extremum maximum power point. Therefore, the M control of local shadow based on intelligent algorithm is becoming more and more popular. However, the conventional intelligent algorithm also has the disadvantage of falling into a local maximum and introducing a large tracking oscillation to the MPPT control system. To solve these problems, this paper proposes an MPPT control strategy based on niche kinetic-molecular theory optimization algorithm (NKMTOA), which combines the ability of niche to jump out of local extremum and the simplicity and efficiency of KTMOA algorithm. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can track more accurately and faster, with smaller oscillation at the maximum power point and higher energy conversion rate, which can track the maximum power point in complex environment in real time.

articleTitle: Sampled-data-based feedback control for a class of switched systems with time delays
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper studies feedback control for a class of switched linear systems with time delays under an event-triggered sampling control link. The sampling is determined by an event-triggered detection condition which is triggered when an error norm turns out bigger than a dynamic state norm. A sufficient solvable condition is developed which can guarantee globally exponential stability of the obtained closed-loop switched delay system. Finally, a numerical example is presented to show the effectiveness and advantage of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: A Methodology for 4D Trajectory Optimization of Arrival Aircraft in Trajectory Based Operation
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Trajectory based operation (TBO) is a future operational concept for the air traffic management. This paper focuses on the trajectory optimization for the arrival phase in the TBO environment. The trajectory management process for future operation of arrival phase is described firstly. Then, an optimization schedule model is proposed to assign conflict-free controlled times of arrival (CTAs) at the key waypoints for aircraft. The average arrival delay, flight distance in terminal and balance of runway traffic flow are considered in the proposed model. The speed profile adjustment algorithm based on the assigned CTA is also presented. Finally, the simulation results at Beijing capital international airport is shown to valid the effectiveness of the developed trajectory optimization method.

articleTitle: Guaranteed Cost Control for Coupling Two-PMSMs Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The guaranteed cost control problem for two permanent magnet synchronous motors(PMSMs) systems with uncertain nonlinear coupling is addressed. First, an accurate dynamic model is developed for the system by explicitly taking into account the nonlinear coupling with uncertainty. Then, a sufficient condition for the stabilization of direct feedback controller is given in terms of linear matrix inequalities(LMIs). Next, a guaranteed cost state feedback controller is developed. Finally, the velocity tracking performance and smaller control cost have been described to verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach in simulations.

articleTitle: The Design of The Fuse Collinear Primer Set System
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: For the characteristics that the firing pin of ammunition fuse collinear primer setting system of large caliber rocket is shared by setting and firing signals, the information setting security must be ensured in the setting process to prevent misfire caused by for the excess current. Besides, information crosslinking task should be completed in the prescribed time. In view of the above problems, high security the collinear primer set system was designed in this paper. The charging and discharging formula were deduced. Besides, the process of charging and discharging system and the information crosslinking are analyzed on the basis of theoretical analysis combining with experiment. The energy was limited in the transmission process. On the basis of safety, the energy storage module stores enough energy. And the information transmission is faster than before. The experimental results were in agreement with the theoretical analysis in this paper. The system provides a technical reference for the fuse collinear primer set.

articleTitle: Modeling and Control Simulation of Giant Magnetostrictive Actuator with Two-end Outputs
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: A kind of giant magnetostrictive actuator (GMA) with two-end outputs is designed. The mechanical structure and its working principle are presented, and the static characteristic experiment of the GMM rod is adopted to determine the linear working range. Based on the above, the mathematical model of the GMA is established according to the piezomagnetic equation and Newton's second law. Then the research on response performance of the open-loop system is executed and the results indicate that the overshoot and the settling time are relatively large. To improve the dynamic response speed and the steady-state output performance, the PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">μ</sup> controller is designed to form a closed-loop control system. The simulation study on the control performance of the closed-loop system is carried out in this paper. When the PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">μ</sup> controller is adopted, the results demonstrate good control performance with an overshoot of step response of 1.77% and a settling time of 2.73×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> s.

articleTitle: Fusion Estimation of States and Faults for Switched Interconnected Systems with Local Networks and Sojourn Probabilities
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The fusion estimation problem of both states and faults is presented for switched interconnected discrete-time systems with local networks and known sojourn probabilities. Two types of fusion estimators, non-weighted and weighted fusion estimators, are presented. By means of the Lyapunov stability theory, sufficient conditions for the existence of both non-weighted and weighted fusion estimators are established. The fusion parameters are computed by solving a convex optimization problem.

articleTitle: Analysis of Frequency Power Characteristics Based on Large Power Grid Data
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Frequency is an important indicator of the safe and stable operation of the power system. Due to the current investment in large capacity generating units and the power fluctuation of new energy sources in the network, the composition of the system is more complicated and the diversity and unpredictability of the changing factors. In this paper, the primary frequency modulation mode of power system is introduced, and the static stability in large power grid is analyzed. The relationship between power shortfall and frequency variation is studied when the degree of load variation is small. The conjecture is analyzed and verified by the measured data of a large power grid. The actual large-scale power grid dispatching and predicting the safe and stable operation of the power grid provide the possibility of using the frequency space to absorb new energy sources.

articleTitle: Dynamic Trajectory Planning of 4-DOF Planar Direct Drive Robot
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Aiming at the requirement of high speed and high accuracy of robot in the field of IC, the current robots has elastic creep and cannot achieve high dynamic response, in this paper, a 4-DOF planar direct drive robot is studied, and a trajectory planning algorithm with the transition of trigonometric function is designed to solve the robot's current existing these problems. Finally, ADAMS is used to simulate the algorithm. Through the research of this paper, the dynamic response of robot is greatly improved.

articleTitle: Satellite Constellation Navigation Method based on Inter-satellite Link and Inter-satellite Orientation
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The ability of autonomous navigation is one of the key features supporting autonomous operation of the satellite constellation. Based on inter-satellite link ranging, the increase of direction observation can obtain the indirect measurements of orbital plane orientation parameters, which determine the absolute direction of the constellation in inertial space, and control the overall drift influence of the constellation orbital elements, thus eliminate the navigation error caused by the overall rotation of the constellation. Simulation results show that the presented method is feasible and can guarantee the long-term navigation accuracy of the satellite constellation.

articleTitle: Analysis of Dead Reckoning Accuracy in Swarm Robotics System
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to determine the position of a single mobile robot in a swarm using dead reckoning techniques. We investigate the accuracy of navigation by using this process. The paper begins with the research background and social importance. Then, the specific experimental setup and analysis of experimental results are presented. Finally, the results are detailed and some potential improvements are provided.

articleTitle: Low Order Sliding Mode Repetitive Control for Discrete-time System under Multi-periodic Disturbances
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: A control method for discrete-time system is proposed. Both the advantages of sliding mode control method and repetitive control method are utilized. It can deal with a discrete-time system that present multi-periodic disturbances. When parameters change, the sliding mode control method is utilized to ensure robustness. Meanwhile, when there are multi-periodic disturbances which frequences are known, low order repetitive control can annihilate them. The effectiveness of proposed method is validated by simulations.

articleTitle: Research on Data Fusion Technology of Map and Sea Chart for Mission Planning System
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In order to meet the application needs of mission planning system using land-sea fusion digital map platform, aiming at the key problems that need to be solved in land-sea geospatial data fusion, this paper proposed the methods of multisource geospatial data fusion and geographic feature classification and coding fusion and fusion preprocessing. Then, the methods of the spatial data model design, coordinate system and projection mode uniformities, feature and coding classification were given. Finally, the spatial vector data fusion of land-sea digital map simulation demo software system was designed to achieve the data fusion between land map and chart. Software demonstration effect validates the effectiveness of land-sea map data fusion method design.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation for Large Span Transmission Broken Lines
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The sudden breakage of conductor enables the quick release of tension in conductor, which causes the dynamic impact effect on transmission line system. For the disconnection problem of large span transmission lines, the finite element model of transmission line tower line system of power transmission tower is built by using of ANSYS software, and the fracture vibration of transmission tower, transmission line and transmission line system are simulated and analyzed. The displacement response curves under impulse loads were given. The simulation results show that the correctness of the modeling results.

articleTitle: Dynamic Gesture Recognition Algorithm based on ROI and CNN for Social Robots
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: To eliminate barriers to communication between social robots and disabled people in listening and/or speaking, this work proposes a gesture recognition method that is based on the region of interest (ROI) and a convolutional neural network (CNN) for social robots. This method can track and recognize gestures in real time in a complex background. ROI and OpenCV are first used to obtain the dynamic gesture, which is then treated as the input of a CNN model to output a gesture feature model. Furthermore, a gesture-controlled social robot is implemented by the obtained feature model. Finally, the performance of the system is verified, and experimental results show that the proposed technology can track and recognize user gestures in real time.

articleTitle: Adaptive Impulsive Hybrid Synchronization of Fractional order Complex Dynamic Network
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, a self-adaptive impulsive mixed synchronization of fractional order compound dynamical network is researched. Firstly, according to the generalized Barbalat’s Lemma, we gained some synchronization guidelines of self-adaptive impulsive mixed control. Then the whole network can be forced to certain desired synchronous state by adaptive impulsive hybrid control strategy. Secondly taking the fractional order Chen chaotic systems as the network nodes and the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is verified by numerical simulation. Finally, the effect about fractional order variation of the synchronization speed is investigated.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-based Robust Adaptive Control for FFSGR with Actuator Deadzone
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper studies the trajectory tracking control problem of free-form surface grinding robot(FFSGR) subjects to asymmetric actuator deadzones, with the presence of friction forces and model uncertainties, and disturbance. The stability of the closed-loop system and the asymptotic convergences of tracking errors are proved using Lyapunov theory. Simulation results show that the deadzone nonlinearity can be estimated correctly. The system trajectory tracking performance can be converge to the desired one since the effect caused by deadzone is eliminated by the control method.

articleTitle: Automatic Integration of Medical Information (AIMI) in cardio-thoracic surgery
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)

authors.preferredName: Robert A. F. de Lind van Wijngaarden

abstract: To make team-based decision during surgery, it is vital that every team member receives the same information. This can only be done by sharing information (input from every team member). With this tool, a foundation for better information input and team communication and decision can be made. This will promote a safer environment for the patient. This research project, taking action in LUMC (Leiden University Medical Center), focusses on solutions of gathering and integrating data generated by the different machines and team members, including a design for new operating room together with a brief introduction of auto-checkout list and a reminder APP in concept.

articleTitle: Analysis of operational capability of military organizations based on improved FINC
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: When analyzing the performance of complex military organizations, it is very important to describe the entities and relationships between entities. The FINC method has many advantages in this aspect. However, with the further application, this method also presents some deficiencies, such as this method is mainly a linear analysis method. In this paper, taking advantage of the timed influence nets (TIN), and considering the actual situation in military operations, this paper improves the calculation process of FINC by adopting the advantage of TIN. The experimental results show that the effective information quality, the collaborative attack capability between fire units and the executive ability calculated by the improved method can better reflect the actual combat situations.

articleTitle: Quantification Analysis of Time Series Based on 2D Visibility State Plot
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Time series analysis is of significant importance with various engineering applications. Inspired by the idea of recurrence quantification analysis (RQA), a novel quantification time series analysis method based on 2D visibility state plot is proposed. In particular, if the two arbitrary data satisfy the visibility criterion, and consequently become two connected nodes of the associated visibility state plot (VSP). Next, In order to quantitatively analyze the VSP, six measures, i.e., visibility rate (VR), degree of certainty (DC), mean diagonal length (DL), visibility entropy (VE), layered (LAY), vertical/horizontal line length (VHL), are calculated. Finally, to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, we compare the performance of our approach to the RQA method using wind speed signals of two different environments. The results show that the quantitative measures of VSP can distinguish indoor and outdoor signals, but the classical RQA method fail to work.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of High Accuracy Current Measurement Circuit Based on Resistance Sampling Method
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Aiming at the requirement of high accuracy measurement of the output current of the gyro in the field of aerospace, military and scientific research. The principle of current measurement and theories of error compensation are studied in this paper. Then a high accuracy current measurement circuit based on the analysis is designed and implemented in this paper. After the error compensation the measurement accuracy of the system is 1.5*10-4 amps when the area of the measurement is ± 0.5 amps. Consequently, this system could provide dynamic high-accuracy measurement of current. The system could be a helpful reference for accuracy current measurement in industrial automation.

articleTitle: Evolutionary Game Model for Data Aggregation Precision in Wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Aiming at the precision problem of data fusion technology in wireless sensor networks (WSNs), an evolutionary game model based on the precision of data fusion is proposed in this paper. The model has fully considered the topology changes resulting from the attack and from the energy problem. The model has also considered the strategy selection problem of selfish nodes in data fusion process. Dynamically evolutionary replication equations based on the precision of data fusion are presented in this paper. According to the strategy selection of the selfish nodes and the dynamic evolution of precision, the incentive mechanism is introduced. We propose and prove the theorems of evolutionarily stable strategy under different parameters. We verify the effects of the incentive mechanism and that the model can optimize the number of nodes in the process of data fusion, reduce the loss caused by the collision of data, and improve the precision of data fusion by simulation.

articleTitle: Active disturbance rejection control for closed-loop gas flow facilities
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Gas flow facilities are essential to test gas flow sensors, meters and other devices. Pressure control is a key problem in particular for high pressure gas flow facilities. An appropriate control scheme is critical to improve the stability and the speed of the pressure control. This paper presents a linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC) scheme for high pressure gas flow facilities with closed-loop pipelines. The control model of the flow facility is identified by a step response method. A reduced-order linear expansion state observer and a related control law are designed to estimate and compensate the total disturbance of the system. The robustness of the ADRC algorithm is compared with a PID control algorithm by Monte Carlo simulation. Control speed and disturbance rejection ability of ADRC are also compared with PID through simulation and gas flow experiments. The results show that, compared with PID, ADRC has a shorter settling time, stronger disturbance rejecting capability and more robust performance. The improved pressure stability has been proved to be beneficial to test gas flow sensors in the facility.

articleTitle: Road Self-adaptive Hybrid Control of Vehicle Semi-active Suspension
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: An acquisition of the road disturbance property is essential for the realization of vehicle suspension road self-adaptive hybrid control systems. The focus of this paper is to apply the road classification algorithm to achieve road pavement adaptation of semi-active suspension hybrid damping control. Firstly, a road contour detection method based on the linear Kalman filter theory is proposed, which has the advantages of high-precision and low-delay in vehicle online control. Secondly, the road pavement grade classifier is designed to divide the estimated road pavement contour. The classifier takes into account both the road pavement contour frequency and its amplitude, whose effectiveness is verified by simulation analysis in Matlab. Lastly, according to the values of the amplitude and frequency, road pavement contour is classified into six ranges. The classification method realizes the hybrid damping control parameters automatically adjust according to the road pavement, in order to obtain better vehicle performance.

articleTitle: Improved Event-Triggered Consensus Control for Multi-Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, we propose centralised consensus control approach based on event-triggered control for multi-agent systems (MASs). Firstly, a centralised event-triggered mechanism is designed to achieve consensus of MASs. Secondly, event interval analysis of the MAS is given to prove there is no Zeno behavior. Next, the self-triggered control is provided to reduce the energy of sampling. Then, we provide the adaptive event-triggered mechanism of the MASs considering the value of measurement error. Finally, an example is presented to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed control methods.

articleTitle: A Loop Closure Detection Method Using Binary Feature Descriptors
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of loop closure detection in simultaneous localization and mapping for mobile robots, we propose a method based on ORB features and BOW model. We extract binary features from the required pictures, then modify a traditional k-means structure according to the characteristics of binary words, obtain the visual dictionary online. The similarity of images can be computed based on the visual words. A Bayesian filter was introduced to select final loop images to guarantee the success rate of the closed-loop detection. Finally, an Epipolar Constraint is performed to remove the wrong images. The proposed approach is detected in several datasets, and the effectiveness of the method is demonstrated by the comparison with several classical algorithms.

articleTitle: Oscillation Characteristics of Feedforward Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Based on the physiological characteristics of the acupuncture signal transduction pathway, this paper uses the Izhikevich model and the small-world neural network to establish a feed forward neural network model to study the influence of the noise of intensity and the connection probability between layers on the oscillation characteristics of the feed forward neural network when the neurons are in the types of regular spiking and burst spiking.

articleTitle: Research on the performance of single CORS positioning system
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Continuous operating reference system (CORS) system has been a hot area of research for domestic and international scholars, its high-precision and stable operation can provide users with continuous, reliable and convenient location guidance service. From practice view, the statistical phenomenon analysis regarding known point RTK positioning was observed, which aims to summarize the self-constructed single CORS' critical performance including precision and consistence philosophy and forms the complete performance analysis theory against single CORS. Continuous observed results indicate: within the scope, cm-accuracy can be achieved with single CORS RTK position algorithm, moreover the horizontal accuracy within 5 cm and Z direction accuracy within 8 cm, the data validity above 99.2%; while its performance decrease dramatically and its initialization time increase obviously when rover exceeds CORS valid scope.

articleTitle: Analysis and Application on Measured Ground Motion Data from Blasting
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In view of the potential risk and disaster caused by the unreasonable controlling measures during blasting work, ground motion experiments under two in situation blasting were carried out. Based on ground motion data acquired from blasting experiments, analysis of time-frequency characteristics is carried out. Frequency spectrum of velocity and acceleration is obtained by using FFT method. Then general law of spectrum distribution of ground motion signal at different blasting distance is obtained. The result shows that the velocity and acceleration data of two blasting experiments were highly similar to each other in time and frequency domain, and the frequency distribution concentrated in lower frequency band if the position is farther away from the detonation center. Empirical calculation formula of the peak velocity is obtained by fitting the ground motion data using the Sadolski method which can provide reference for the following blasting work.

articleTitle: Parallelism Enhancing Cellular Communication - on Knowledge City Evolving
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The knowledge and information infrastructure, especially its health and security protection being not negotiated, can be related for national development, and evidenced in traditional Chinese shuyuans being as knowledge centers. To evolve contemporary knowledge economy, holistic, inclusive, information interactions are getting more importance. Plural (dual) surveillance which is rooted in biologic senses, e.g., from two-eyes, can have the feature of fault-tolerance, availability and maintainability in monitoring tasks. It can fit the contemporary wireless communication methods being incorporated with MIMO (multi-in multi-out), to prevent information loss, interference, unexpected changes caused by such as clogged water. Network prototypes, including SW (spider-web) and CCC (cube-connected cycle) networks, are proactively suggested for evolving information based development. Furthermore, the mutually independent Hamiltonian Path (MIHP) property of SW can be used for parallel analyzing interference and supporting cypher coding to offer privacy. Similarly, other networks, such as the Honeycomb tori, can offer an alternative pattern.

articleTitle: Optimal ultracapacitor permutation and combination for voltage equalization using Rejected Monte Carlo algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Ultracapacitors are novel energy storage devices with high power density and long cycle life. For practical applications, numerous ultracapacitor monomers need to be connected in series or parallel to form modules, in which the voltage imbalance among monomers induced by technological parameter dispersion would damage ultracapacitors. It is an important issue to achieve the voltage balance with lower energy cost. Instead of designing cell balancing systems to minimize the voltage imbalance, this paper proposes a method for optimized ultracapacitor permutation and combination using Rejected Monte Carlo algorithm. This method not only reduces voltage difference, but also decreases balancing current and energy loss of the equalization circuit. Simulation results are provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Active Disturbance Rejection Control for an Omnidirectional Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, a nonlinear active disturbance rejection controller is applied for the trajectory tracking control of an omnidirectional mobile robot under dynamic uncertainties and external disturbances. A dynamic model of an omnidirectional mobile robot (OMR) is derived. The generalized proportional integral (GPI) observer is used to estimate the dynamic uncertainties and external disturbances. A nonlinear proportional derivative (NPD) controller is applied to control the OMR for achieving excellent performances in the trajectory tracking missions. The stability of the control system is analyzed. Simulation results are presented to show the effectiveness of the nonlinear active disturbance rejection controller.

articleTitle: Boundedness Analysis on Large Signal Average Model of Full-Bridge DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: For the full-bridge DC-DC converter, the operating points vary with the load. It is important to confirm the boundedness on the basis of the large signal average model. In this paper, the full-bridge converter with block capacitor is the subject investigated. Firstly, the large signal average model added into the correction factors is founded and formulated. The process of modeling is similar to that of converter with LLC circuit. Secondly, the boundedness analysis on the model is described so that whether the model is bounded or not can be judged. The two signals A and B directly impact the boundedness of other state variables. Lastly but very important, the numerical and experimental results are both used to verify the boundedness of the converter. No matter the load is constant or the step change, the model and the converter are always bounded. What is more, compared with the first harmonic approximation (FHA), the theoretical analysis on the model is more in accordance with the actual converter.

articleTitle: Simulation Model Framework Design for Complex Communication Network of Satellite Navigation System Based on SMP2.0
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The Complex Communication Network of Satellite Navigation System (SNS-CCN) possesses the characteristics such as large scale, complicated architecture, integrated satellite-earth and etc. According to the simulation of information flow for SNS-CCN, this paper proposes a composite framework of simulation model based on SMP2.0 while applied with combination modeling methods. In order to support both the component structure and the simulation service structure, we bring forward the corresponding composite modeling development and integration method. In the end, this paper gives an illustration to develop the component models and to verify the availability of the model framework.

articleTitle: Keypoint Matching Outlier Removal with 3DMP Histogram Voting
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Keypoint matching is a fundamental work in many feature-based vision-related robotic applications, such as image frame tracking and loop closing verification in SLAM (Simultaneously Localization and Mapping). For removing outliers in raw matching results, in contrast to traditional methods like RANSAC, we develop a simpler and more efficient method, by extending the exiting method known as histogram voting. Inspired by the spatial statistic constraint of the small camera motion assumption in optical flow, a fact could be drawn that the pairs of correctly matched keypoints should yield displacement of a well-defined distribution, not only in image coordinates, but in keypoint orientation (3D). With the 3D displacement statistics, a histogram is built for identifying the matching inliers, in which multiple peaks (MP) instead of one are picked for selecting inlier candidates. In both cases of closed loop with significant illumination changes and view-angle changes, our method shows competitive or better performance than traditional RANSAC methods or previously proposed histogram voting methods, validated by experiments on open outdoor datasets and our own experimental environment.

articleTitle: An improved screening method based on standard Morris for learning neural network
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The learning neural network (LNN) has shown good performance in prediction and regression fields, because the number of hidden neurons can be adjusted and the structure can be trained to fit any unknown function. However, those redundant hidden neurons may make the structure of LNN complicated, which is likely to increase the computational cost and time consumption.
