articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Task-oriented Rotor-flying Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Rotor-flying manipulator system is a new type of unmanned aerial vehicle which consists of a multirotor platform and a multi-degree-of-freedom arm attached underneath. The high performance system with advanced manipulation capability can physically interact with the environment and achieve aerial operation autonomously in complex environment. To resolve the autonomous operation ability of the system in unstructured environment and deal with the strong coupling characteristics between the flight platform and the manipulator, This paper designed and developed a rotor-flying multi-joint manipulator system, including hardware design and assembly, the design of control system and establishment of experimental platform. The dynamic compensation for gravity offset control scheme to ensure the stable flight of system based on the backstepping algorithm. Then guided by onboard vision, an experiment for autonomous grasping is conducted in outdoor environment based on visual servo control scheme.

articleTitle: Pose control of rigid bodies with a distance-dependent communication topology
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The pose control problem of rigid bodies is concerned with designing control laws such that their positions and attitudes reach a desired shape. This paper considers the pose control problem of moving rigid bodies communicating via a distance-dependent interaction network. The focus is on a class of poses where the inter-distances of the rigid bodies maintain a predefined rigid formation while their attitudes tend to the same. In the design of control laws for each rigid body, the finite-time control and potential function techniques are used. The key in the analysis lies in the coupling relationship between positions and attitudes of all rigid bodies. Some convergence results on the pose synchronization, rigidity formation maintenance and local convergence of rigidity formations are established.

articleTitle: Classification of pathological and non-pathological Cardiodynamicsgram (CDG) using nonlinear dynamics indexes
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Cardiodynamicsgram (CDG) has emerged recently as a new noninvasive recording method of cardiac dynamics information during heart-beating process, which can be used for the early detection of myocardial ischemia. Automatic classification between pathological and non-pathological CDG can assist doctors in identification of the latent myocardial ischemia for their planning of minimizing ischemic time. In this work, we propose a classification methodology to classify pathological and non-pathological CDG. As the cardiac characteristics extracted by conventional morphology analysis methods is relatively limited and not comprehensive enough to reflect the dynamical characteristics of CDG, we extract three nonlinear dynamics indexes which include C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> complexity (C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>), Approximate entropy (ApEn) and Lyapunov-exponent spectrum (LypE) as a measure of the complexity and nonlinearity of CDG in this work. These indexes are inputted into five different classifiers, including Naive bayes classifier (NBC), Support vector mechines (SVM), K-Nearest neighbour classifier (KNN), Multilayer perceptron (MLP), and Decision tree classifier (DTC). Experimental results at Chinese National Center for Cardiovascular Diseases show that encouraging classification accuracy can be achieved. Additionally, the computation time of these indexes extraction and classfication is very short, which is helpful for building up a real-time software tool towards assisting the physician in cardiology departments.

articleTitle: A Constrained Coordination Control Strategy for Multi-Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Coordination control of multi-agent systems has received a great deal of attention and becoming an attractive research subject, in particular, the control problem of formation control with the property of convex hull is one of important aspect that is needed to deal with. In this paper, a decentralized constrained control method was proposed to achieve a specified formation in two dimensional plane using the inter-range between agents, only local knowledge is required, notice that all agents do not interact with each other based on the designed non-linear controller. To this end, suppose agents have the same measure capabilities, as a consequence, for each agent, its neighboring set of agents is created by using its sensing maximum distance, we then investigate the stability of multi-agent system. Finally, to support the theoretical results, some simulation results are provided, and future research directions are also briefly discussed.

articleTitle: Output tracking control for master-slave Boolean control network via a decomposition technology
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper solves output tracking problem of master-slave Boolean control network (MS-BCN) via a decomposition method. To ensure that the slave Boolean network (BN) tracks a constant reference signal, we search for an uncertainty control set and provide a method to determine such an uncertainty control set. Then we focus on the master BN and assign the real controllers to guarantee that all states of the master BN are steered into the uncertainty control set. In dealing with the master BN, we introduce two different methods to find the largest open-loop control invariant set and closed-loop control invariant set. Finally, an illustrative example shows that the obtained algorithm is effective.

articleTitle: Improved Local Path Planning Base on Grid Map
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The research of unmanned mobile platforms has always been a hot topic and autonomous mobile is one of the key issues. To achieve autonomous mobility, a good path planning is needed. At present, there are many kinds of path planning methods and each has its own advantages and disadvantages.In this paper, an improved local planning method is proposed. Based on the environmental information obtained by the perceptual equipment, the grid map is established. In order to simplify our introduction, the obstacle avoidance task is taken as an example. The main ideas and specific steps of the method are introduced. The simulation experiment is carried out and the advantages and disadvantages of the method are summarized.

articleTitle: Modelling of the Electromagnetic Field Distributions Induced by Different Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Coil Configurations
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: As a brain modulation technology, transcranial magnetic stimulation(TMS) was favored by its particularly advantages such as non-contact, painless, variety stimulation options. There are two TMS coil configurations which was widely used in the clinical research about neurological and psychiatric disorders, and they are the conventional circular coil and figure-8 coil. Based on the same crafts, six different coil configurations with different loop offset distances between the two were proposed in this paper. For the characterization of magnetic and electric field distributions, finite element method was used in an isotropic human brain model and the penetration depth and stimulation focality were regarded as the two most important indicators. Our results support that the figure-S coil has better focality and penetration depth than conventional circular coil in the circumstance where same current pulse was delivered. As the increasing of loop offset distance, there is an obvious law in the focality of induced electric field. The coil which loop offset distance equals to 20 mm has the best focality. A tradeoff between penetration depth and stimulation focality of electric field induced by the six coil configurations was discovered. For the selection of coil setting and the design of novel coil configuration, the evaluation between these two different needs is considerable.

articleTitle: Particle Swarm Optimized Reinforcement Learning-Based Fault Tolerant Control
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Data-driven fault-tolerant controllers have recently gained considerable attention due to their important role in modern technological systems. The reinforcement learning is an attractive tool of data-driven but it is limited to the learning speed. A particle swarm optimization is proposed to improve the learning speed of reinforcement learning by transferring the series computation to parallel operation. The numeric simulation shows it is a feasible approach.

articleTitle: Integral High Order Sliding Mode Control for Servo Turntable
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to design a global robust and finite-time convergent controller for a servo turntable system. High order sliding mode control (HOSMC) with 2-order sliding surface is designed. This novel control method is formulated by using higher order sliding mode control with integral sliding surface applying to an auxiliary system. The controller applied in this paper is based on reaching law and geometric homogeneity approach which can compensate the uncertain environment and ensure finite-time convergence. The finite-time stability and convergence of HOSMC is proved by both the Lyapunov stability and negative homogeneity approach. Simulations and comparisons are conducted for the angle position tracking of servo turntable system. The outcomes with impressive steady state precision and higher convergence speed reveal the effectiveness of the proposed control method in this work.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo Box Node Localization Algorithm for mobile WSN based on Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: An optimization node localization algorithm is proposed for Wireless Sensor Network (WSN). It synthesizes the Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Monte Carlo Box and puts forward one optimized estimated coordinate weight based on the node movement coherence, named as SVMMCB. Towards the localization mechanism, we use SVM to classify the ordinary nodes and get the reasonable Temporary Anchor Nodes (TAN), which are recognized as the nodes which own the lower localization errors and should be localized on the first step, furthermore, to localize the other ordinary nodes with anchor nodes. Meanwhile, in the period of establishing the sample box, we consider the correction radius based on the last time's possible localization error to get the more complete sample area than before. The results of simulation demonstrate that compared with the traditional MCB scheme, the SVMMCB gets the more reasonable TANs, the more accurate sample area and the higher localization accuracy.

articleTitle: Adaptive Iterated Cubature Particle Filter for Mobile Robot Monte Carlo Localization
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of computational burden and poor performance in real time in cubature Monte Carlo localization (CMCL), a novel algorithm is presented in this paper. Firstly, a Cubature Particle Filter (CPF) for generating the importance proposal distribution by Gauss-Newton iterative Cubature Kalman Filter (ICKF) is designed. This algorithm is not limited by the high-order truncation error of ordinary cubature particle filters. Subsequently, enhance CPF by automatically adjusting the particle set size using the Kullback-Leibler Distance (KLD) standard, thereby increasing the speed of the newly proposed Adaptive Iterative CPF (AICPF). Simulation result is compared with standard cubature particle filter which demonstrates that the proposed AICPF is superior to the previous method in estimating the mean square and computational cost of the error. In addition, this study also applies AICPF to robot positioning on robotic operating systems (ROS). An analysis is conducted to confirm feasibility and efficiency of the adaptive iterated cubature MCL (AICMCL), which improves the accuracy of robot localization, and recovers more quickly from interference. It adjusts the number of particles needed for localization in real time, reduces computational burden, and improves the real-time processing capability.

articleTitle: The Design and Research of Data Transmission on Remote Radio Control in Different Noise Channel
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Previously a novel chaotic transmission method was proposed in air traffic voice communication system, which was applied in remote radio control transmission. It has better performance than Frequency Shift Keying in transmission efficiency, bandwidth efficiency, and anti-additive-white-noise performance. However, the channel noise in communication has great effect on the proposed transmission method. Thus the problem of chaotic modulated signals affected by channel noise and how to design chaotic M-ary communication system in additive color Gauss noise for data transmission are studied in this paper. Firstly, chaotic modulated signals' boundary range affected by additive white Gauss noise is studied and the formula is derived. Then, the design of chaotic receiver in additive color Gauss noise channel is given, and the construction method on how to design anti-additive-color-Gauss-noise chaotic communication system is proposed. Finally the simulation result shows the correctness of chaotic receiver boundary range formula, the proposed method in this paper can improve the anti-additive-color-gauss-noise performance of data transmission, it provides a new way for remote radio control data transmission.

articleTitle: Discrete-Time Fractional Order Integral Sliding Mode Control for Piezoelectric Actuators with Improved Performance Based on Fuzzy Tuning
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, the discrete-time fractional order integral sliding mode control design for linear uncertain systems is investigated. First, a new method is proposed to approximate the fractional order integral recursively. Then, the control design based on the proposed approximation is presented. Finally, the fuzzy tuning which adjusts the integral gain and the fractional order of the integral simultaneously is employed to improve the transient response of the control system. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy is verified by both simulations and experiments on a piezo-actuated positioning system.

articleTitle: PSO Hammerstein Model Based PM2.5 Concentration Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: With the continuous improvement of living standards and the progress of science and technology, the problems of air pollution are very serious and research on the forecasting of PM2.5 concentration is particularly important. In this paper, we describe the development of a method to forecast the daily average PM2.5 concentration of Ningbo. The research is based upon the measurements from eight urban center monitoring sites during the period of 2013-2014. By normalizing the sample data and using the PCA method to reduce the its dimension, a multi-input single-output Hammerstein model for forecasting the concentration of PM2.5 is established by using PSO algorithm to identify the parameters of the model. According to the results reported here, the PSO Hammerstein model can be used to predict the PM2.5 concentration of regional air well.

articleTitle: An Explicit Analytical Estimation of the Validity of the Tanimoto Similarity by Confidence Intervals in Mathematical Statistics
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In order to evaluate the validity of the Tanimoto similarity in the fields of machine learning and data mining rigorously, the “validity” is interpreted as the term of confidence intervals of a point estimation in mathematical statistics, if the sets inputted into Tanimoto similarity are extended to two finite random variable samples. The range of confidence intervals (the lower bound subtracts from the upper bound) gets smaller, the validity gets more valid. Based on the existing references, an explicit analytical expression from the Pearson correlation coefficient to the Tanimoto similarity is deduced. The Fisher transformation is employed to estimate the confidence intervals of the sample Pearson correlation coefficient. Then the confidence intervals of the Tanimoto similarity are generated, if the lower bound and the upper bound is substituted into the explicit analytical expression respectively. Numerical experiments confirm the veracity of the explicit analytical expression. In the ultra-short term wind speed prediction by spatial correlation, the root mean square error of wind speed prediction is decreased by about 17%, if substitute the Tanimoto similarity for the Pearson correlation coefficient to sort out the most similar neighbors in the k-nearest neighbor prediction model. To improve the accuracy and reliability of wind power prediction in the green renewable energy field, the Tanimoto similarity is much better than the Pearson correlation coefficient in the correlation estimation between the wind speeds.

articleTitle: An Online Parameter Identification for Ultracapacitor Model by Using Recursive Least Square with Multi-forgetting Factor
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Reliable parameters information is of great importance for on-board energy management and optimal power control. In this paper, we applies the online strategy of multi-forgetting factor recursive least square algorithm to identify parameters of first-order dynamic model through cyclic operating current. The output voltage of the identified model shows a good agreement with the experimental results, and the results of comparison with curve fitting method highlight the proposed method has great accuracy and convergence.

articleTitle: Hybrid Modeling and Control Strategy for High Boost DC/DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Aiming at the characteristics of on and off in switching devices of power converters, the hybrid switching characteristics of High Boost DC/DC(HB) converter are described by the hybrid system theory. In this paper, the characteristic of HB converter working in a cycle is introduced in detail, and its hybrid automaton model is established based on the hybrid system theory. The energy conservation principle is used to deduce the boundary condition of switching during the system operation in CCM mode. To verify the correctness of theoretical analysis, the control algorithm is further explored by MATLAB simulation software. The simulation results show that this method has the advantages of simple control algorithm and fast dynamic response.

articleTitle: The optimization of ET by FCM and Its Variants
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Electrical Tomography (ET) is an advanced process detecting technique, but its spatial resolution is too low to be applied in most practical engineering fields. Some algorithms have been proposed to enhance ET spatial resolution, but the problem of trail traces remains unsolved to a great extent. In this paper, we apply fuzzy clustering to ET imaging process. Depending on the grays from the existing ET algorithms, the trail traces in ET images can efficiently be reduced. This proposed method has been tested by a group of simulations and a group of experiments. The results show that this new method can efficiently improve the spatial resolution of ET images and provide a new choice for ET imaging process.

articleTitle: Cooperative Nonlinear Output Regulation of Multi-agent Systems with Uncertain Leader
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this work, we investigate the cooperative output regulation problem of multi-agent uncertain nonlinear systems in lower triangular form with unknown leader. The cooperative output regulator construction is done based on a nonlinear internal model approach. Specifically, nonlinear internal models are first constructed, converting the cooperative output regulation problem into a cooperative stabilization problem of the augmented system, and then an integral input-to-state stable (iISS) based approach is proposed to solve the latter cooperative stabilization. It finally gives rise to a constructive state feedback design for cooperative nonlinear output regulation problem.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification of an Aerodynamic Olfactory Effect Model for the Simulation of Gas-Sensitive Rotorcrafts
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper described an experiment which was designed to validate the effectiveness of an aerodynamic olfactory effect model for the simulation of gas-sensitive rotorcrafts. The model simulates the rotor wakes using free vortices and calculates the distortion of the gas plume using filament based plume model. We designed an experiment in which a camera recorded the distortion of the smoke plume, and proposed a practical video processing routine to extract the smoke dispersion trajectory. Then the trajectory was compared with the simulated one to validate the model. Results showed that this aerodynamic olfactory effect model is a credible way to simulate odor diffusion process under the influence of quadrotor.

articleTitle: Geometry-based Mass Grading of Betelnut Using Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper presents a system for betelnut shapes grading into four classes according to standards stipulated in China. The system effectively obtains the semi-major axis, semi-minor axis, perimeter, area and other characteristic parameters of betelnut through edge detection, and obtains the grade of each parameter of betelnut based on the subordinate function classification method, and then comprehensively evaluates the level of betelnut according to the weighted algorithm. The results show that the betelnut size detection error is not more than 5%,and the shape classification accuracy is above 90%. The average time to grade one betelnut is below 450ms.

articleTitle: Design of PWM Subdivision Driver for Multi-axis Stepper Controlling
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In order to realize high-precision subdivision driving and multi-axis controlling for stepper motor system, a new PWM subdivision driver with multi-axis controlling is proposed. It mainly contains four independent PWM subdivision driving modules with Avalon bus interface, which can be used to set the working mode in each PWM channel for different motion axis. Each PWM subdivision driving module can output PWM square wave with maximum 256 subdivision, and can work in continuous or limited, synchronous or asynchronous working mode. Two or more PWM subdivision driving modules can be set to synchronize the PWM output, which realizes multi- axis controlling. The new PWM subdivision driver is designed by Verilog HDL language, simulated in Modelsim, and verified by using DE2-115 FPGA development board connected to four stepper motors via LMD18200 H Bridges. Both simulation and experiment results show that each PWM subdivision driving module can generate high-precision PWM square wave for different subdivision setting in continuous or limited working mode, and can work stably in cooperation for multi-axis control.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation Analysis of a Novel Outer Rotor IPM Motor Used in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Aiming at the distributed drive system of electric vehicles, this paper presents an outer-rotor permanent-magnet synchronous in-wheel motor with a novel U-shape rotor structure. Instead of the traditional surface-mounted permanent-magnet structure, adopting the U-shape interior permanent magnet (IPM) structure is beneficial to improving the performance of the in-wheel motor of electric vehicles (EVs). The finite element analysis (FEA) models of the U-shape interior permanent magnet motor and the surface-mounted permanent-magnet motor are both established to compare. The results show that the novel U-shape interior permanent-magnet motor not only reduces the amount of permanent magnet, but also improves the back electromotive force (EMF), torque output, flux weakening capability and reduces the cogging torque. The research shows that the U-shape interior permanent magnet motor is better suited to the requirements of the motor used in electric vehicles, and provides some reference for the design of the in-wheel motor of electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Stabilization of Minimum-Phase Linear Uncertain Systems With Quantized Measurement Output and Disturbances
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, we study the robust stabilization problem of minimum-phase linear uncertain systems with the quantized measurement output and external disturbances. Although the stabilization problem of linear systems by quantized feedback control has been well addressed, the robust stabilization problem subject to external disturbances by quantized feedback control is still an open problem. It is quite challenging to tackle the system uncertainty and external disturbances by quantized output feedback. By Lyapunov analysis, we design a dynamic quantized output feedback control law to solve the problem. In contrast to existing results where the input-to-state stability with respect to external disturbances is attained for the linear system by quantized state feedback control, the asymptotic stability of the linear system is achieved in the presence of system uncertainties and disturbances by the dynamic quantized output feedback control law.

articleTitle: Event-triggered output feedback control with quantized state observer
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, combining the event-triggered mechanism and the quantized observer, an output feedback control approach is proposed for networked control systems. In such control systems, firstly, the observer is used to estimate the state of the system when an event is triggered. Next, the observer state is firstly quantized and then transmitted to the controller for feedback. Moreover, it has been proved that the closed-loop system can achieve asymptotic stable if a prescribed set of linear matrix inequalities is satisfied. Finally, a simulation example is given to illustrate the efficiency of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Effect of inhibitory firing patterns on the stochastic resonance in feed-forward-loop neuronal network motifs
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Neurons express diverse firing patterns in terms of their morphological, biochemical and electrophysiological properties. Different firing patterns can switch the information transmission in neuron network. However, it is not clear how the firing patterns of the neurons affect information transmission. Here we investigate the effect of different firing patterns of inhibitory neuron on network information transmission of triple-neuron feed-forward-loop motif. Results show that the stochastic response behavior can be optimized by certain noise intensity, which indicates stochastic resonance (SR) occurs in the neuronal network motifs. Changing the inhibitory neuron from burst spiking neurons to fast spiking neurons does not affect the optimal noise intensity. In the case of the same noise intensity and coupling coefficient, the bursting neurons produce higher transmission efficiency than the fast firing neurons. Different firing patterns of neuron in the output of the network motif achieved a greater impact on the transmission efficiency of the motif than the neuron located in the middle position. This simulation directly quantifies the influence of firing patterns on information transmission, which has great significance for improving signal transmission efficiency and detecting signals at different operating points.

articleTitle: An Improved Nonlinear Tracking Differentiator and its Application
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: An improved nonlinear tracking differentiator(INTD) with limited control variable is proposed in this paper. Compared with the existing high speed nonlinear tracking differentiators(HSTD), INTD preserves the stability of HSTDs at the target state and their rapidity. In particular, the HSTD's problem of poor anti-interference ability and narrow application range is solved by INTD. This paper analyzes the tracking performance of INTD with different threshold coefficient of control variable and processing different step signals under the same threshold coefficient. It is verified that HSTD needs a proper limit for control variable. INTD is applied to process the magnetic phase signal of maglev train position and speed detection system, the result shows that this improved nonlinear tracking differentiator can well track and filtering phase angle signal.

articleTitle: A Spectral Radiant Heat Flux Calculation Model For Stratospheric Airships
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: A spectral radiant heat flux calculation model for stratospheric airships is constructed in this paper. First, the net heat method is applied and developed by further considering the effect of the gas inside the airship, the transmission of the skin and the spectral properties of the radiation sources. The calculation methods of different spectral radiation sources are introduced and the mathematical model of the absorption coefficient of the internal gas is built. Then the net heat method is simplified to improve the computational efficiency. At last, an example is taken to show the radiant heat flux distribution on the skin of the airship, meanwhile to verify the validity of the simplified net heat method. The radiant heat flux distribution on the skin of the stratospheric airship in different regions of spectrum are shown, the result also shows that the sun provides important radiation in the infrared spectrum.

articleTitle: Sliding-mode Dynamic Surface Adaptive Path-following of Unmanned Vessels with Dynamic Uncertainties and Disturbances
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: A novel line-of-sight (LOS) based sliding-mode dynamic surface adaptive (SDSA) scheme is presented for the path-following of unmanned surface vessels (USVs) with uncertain parameters and constant disturbances. The inertia and damping matrixes of the USV are maintaining asymmetry such that it remains higher accuracy of model. Introducing the coordinate transformation to system matrixes so that turned it into skew-symmetrical form. One separates the guidance-control design procedure into two stages, guidance subsystem and control subsystem, respectively. At the first stage, considering improved LOS algorithm to ensure USV effectively sufficient following the predefined path, with the approximately calculated method of sideslip. At the second stage, using the velocity dynamics to design the surge force and yaw moment. Sliding-mode dynamic surface and adaptive techniques are adopted to compensate for uncertain parameters and constant bias caused by environmental disturbances. In particularly, the dynamic surface overcome the explosion of complexity. It is shown that the close-loop system is uniformly asymptotically stable by using Lyapunov stability and cascade stability theories. Simulation results illustrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed scheme by a full-scale tanker and a small vessel model with the same controller parameters.

articleTitle: A Multi-actuator Soft Robot Inspired by Young Tiger Beetle
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The young tiger beetle has flexible body and two tough pliers, it can capture and kill a bug in seconds. The paper present the design of a multi-actuator soft robot based on detailed morphological and kinematic investigations of young tiger beetle. 3D printing technology is used to fabricate the crawling, steering and occluding structures. Three actuators are designed to mimic complex movement of the young tiger beetle. Actuator one and actuator two are used to control the movement and turning, and actuator three is used to mimic the bite action. Experiments are carried out to verify the designed multi-actuator soft robot.

articleTitle: Decision Tree combining with the Attribute Reduction Algorithm for Substation Alarm Processing
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In order to process the uncertain information of the substation alarms, the traditional Decision Tree Method is improved. The redundant signals in alarm sequence are simplified with the algorithm based on Positive Domain Attribute Reduction, the result of which is used as the characteristic attribute of the Decision Tree. Meanwhile, by constructing the Decision Tree in cooperated with temporal logic relation of the alarm signal, the characteristic attribute sequence can be accurately sorted, which finally produces a reasoning result for the alarm analysis. The method proposed in the paper is of concise and reasonable, and is proved having a good effect for fault classification decision making of the substation alarm processing.

articleTitle: Manipulation the Pose of Single Cell by Cooperation of Multiple Optical Manipulators
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Cell surgery is becoming an emerging technology in various biomedical applications. Adjusting the pose of the target cell properly for surgical observation and operations is critical to the success of cell surgery. Unfortunately, cell pose adjustments are usually operated manually, which suffers low operation accuracy and efficiency. In this paper, an automatic cell pose adjustment approach is proposed via the cooperation manipulation of multiple flexible optical manipulators, on the base of a holographic optical tweezers cell manipulation system. A novel geometric model is first established to confine the optical manipulator to keep grasping with the specific position of the target cell by using the concept of flexible manipulator in robotics. Then, a cooperation manipulation algorithm integrated with a unified potential field based controller are design to coordinate multiple flexible optical manipulators to adjust the pose of the target cell to the desired state. Simulation and experiment are performed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Automatic Detection of Bow Echoes from Weather Radar Images
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Bow echo is a kind of convective storm that often associates with swaths of damaging straight-line winds and small tornadoes. When observed using weather radar, visual features of bow echoes includes rear inflow notches and bowing segments, which are useful predictors of damaging straight-line winds. In this paper a method is proposed for automatic detection of bow echoes from single radar reflectivity images. The method first detects quasi-linear convective systems (QLCSs) based on radon transform, then describes the QLCSs using their contour models, and finally identifies concave segments along the tailing edge of the contour models as indicator of bow echoes. These identified concave segments are also used to forecast damaging winds by extrapolating their tracks. The proposed method is demonstrated using two bow echo cases. The results show that bow echoes are successfully detected, and the corresponding damaging winds could be forecasted at least 15 min before the winds occur.

articleTitle: An Efficient Routing Algorithm based on K-means++ Clustering and Fuzzy for Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: A wireless sensor network is an distributed self-organizing network with a number of sensor nodes in the monitoring area. The key issue of developing a wireless sensor network with good performance is how to reduce the energy consumption and prolong the lifetime of the network for seeing that the energy of nodes supplied by batteries are limited. We propose an efficient routing algorithm for wireless sensor network named ERA in this paper. In the ERA, firstly, the whole network are divided in several clusters with clustering algorithm. Then the cluster heads are selected in the corresponding clusters with our designed fuzzy logical system. The simulation illustrates that, comparing with the existed routing algorithms such as LEACH, LEACH-C and SEP, the ERA prolongs the network lifetime (first node dies) by 67%.

articleTitle: A new hybrid approach for short-term water demand time series forecasting
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This study proposed a new hybrid approach for short-term water demand prediction. Raw water demand data were decomposed into a set of intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) component and a residue by using ensemble empirical mode decomposition (EEMD) method. IMF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> is the main random component of the raw water demand data, the continuous deep belief neural network (CDBNN) model is used to predict IMF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>. Other IMFs and residue can be recombined employing autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) model for forecasting, this method reduces forecasting steps without increasing the forecasting error. The final forecasting result was obtained by summing the forecasting results of the two models. A historical hourly water demand data from an urban waterworks of Zhuzhou, China were investigated by the hybrid method. Simulation results indicate that the proposed approach has higher forecasting accuracy than back propagation neural network (BPNN), support vector regression (SVR), EEMD and their combinations.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Electric Vehicles and Isolated Microgrid based on Differential Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper investigates the integrated scheduling of distributed energy resources and electric vehicles in isolated microgrid. The multi-types renewable energy sources management model considering photovoltaic, wind turbine, diesel generator, battery and fuel cell is proposed. The objective of the proposed optimal scheduling problem is to minimize the total cost of operational cost and environmental management cost. Besides differential search algorithm approach to the optimal scheduling problem is applied. A case study with an isolated microgrid including a fleet of electric vehicles is used to illustrate the performance of the differential search algorithm. The results show that the proposed coordinated scheduling strategy of microgrid with electric vehicles satisfies economic goals and differential search algorithm has competitiveness to traditional intelligent algorithm in solution for scheduling of microgrid.

articleTitle: Research on identifying the rear-end conflict risk of highway
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: As the increasing of automobiles, tremendous information on roads need to be deal with, which has become the challenge for the efficiency of the intelligent transportation system. This paper is aimed to improve the efficiency for identifying the risk of conflict in highway and propose an analysis method through a new vision to analyze the car-following safety of highway based on traffic conflict technology instead of historical accident data. Firstly, a term “vehicle-group” is introduced and the algorithm identifying their ranges is presented. And then the risk measurement model for vehicles’ rear-end collision is studied based on time-to-collision (TTC) method. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed model is confirmed by using a case study based on VISSIM simulation. The results show that the screening scope of potential risk can be reduced by identifying the vehicle-groups, which will improve the efficiency of identifying the danger in highway. And this also could provide significant information for the prevention or early warning of chain rear-end collision on roads. Meanwhile, this study has provided a new idea and method for road traffic safety analysis and evaluation research, which will enrich the theory of traffic conflict technology.

articleTitle: Load-following Control of Nuclear Reactors Based on L1 Adaptive Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In order to improve the load-following ability of nuclear reactors, an advanced load-following controller based on L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> adaptive control theory is proposed in this paper. First, the state estimator, which is used to reconstruct the unmeasured state, is built according to the reactor core uncertain model. Then, an adaptive control law is structured to estimate the core uncertainty online while ensuring the global asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system. Finally, L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> adaptive control law is designed to compensate for system uncertainties and ensure that the system realizes load-following control. Considering the high gain problem caused by adaptive control, the low pass filter is added to suppress high frequency oscillation effectively. The simulation results show that the proposed controller is not only adaptive to the system uncertainty, but also effectively completes the load-following control.

articleTitle: An Integrated Estimation Scheme for Resolving Tire Deformation Problem of Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Tire deformation problem of autonomous vehicles can not be neglected for most practical applications due to the complex road conditions, unsmooth motion control inputs, time-varying load weight, etc. This paper presents a novel scheme for on-line state estimation of an autonomous vehicle with tire deformation. Specifically, an adaptive estimator is designed to provide essential positions, velocities, and perturbation estimation of the vehicle by combining the inertial measurements and visual feedback. The convergence properties of the proposed estimator can be theoretically proved. Moreover, the developed estimation scheme can be easily implemented with low-cost onboard sensors. Simulation results validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed estimator in the presence of tire deformation.

articleTitle: Development of Robot Gripper and Force Control
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Generally, robotic gripper enhances the efficiency and the ability to grasp and to control robot`s manipulator rapidly to objects in different shapes and dimensions. In this paper, a new design to control robotic gripper is proposed by controlling based on grasping force method. The gripper is designed with two jaws driven symmetrically by the actuator to grasp and to release the object. Basically, its force is directly measured by force sensing resistance (FSR) type. Force controller is designed by using PID control algorithm with different control gains and objects tuning by experiment methods. Results are shown by experiment by using GUI system. Responses of force controller in different grasping objects are identical. In addition, the virtual motion of robot gripper can be displayed on computer. So this work will lead to improve the grasping force controller design and to enhance working performance in remote environment during handling operation of robot gripper.

articleTitle: Kinematics Features for 3D Action Recognition Using Two-Stream CNN
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Due to the great success of convolutional neural networks (CNN) on image classification problems, several attempts have been made to train deep neural networks for human action recognition problem. But since CNN is designed for static RGB images, it is not easy for it to learn temporal information from videos. To tackle this problem, temporal encoded kinematics features are proposed, which compute the linear velocity and orientation displacement based on human skeleton data. A two-stream CNN architecture is used, incorporating spatial and temporal networks. The spatial ConvNet is trained on still RGB images, while the temporal ConvNet is trained on the proposed encoded kinematics features. We evaluate our method on a popular and challenging 3D multiview human action benchmark, Northwestern-UCLA dataset. The experiment results show that our proposed method is fast to train and performs better when compared to traditional handcrafted features.

articleTitle: FPGA-based spiking neural network with hippocampal oscillation dynamics towards biologically meaningful prostheses
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Hippocampus plays a critical role in human cognitive functions. In this paper a FPGA-based spiking neural network with hippocampal oscillation dynamics is presented with real-time computational speed. The effects of the internal surroundings including the carbachol perfusion have been considered and realized based on FPGA. The effects of the rhythm modulation of the hippocampal neural network are considered, which provides feasibilities to investigate more biological dynamics. In addition, scalable hardware architectures are discussed in detail and provided using multiple hardware techniques. This feasible and efficient design will facilitate the study on the dynamical behaviors of the cognitive function, and is an essential step towards building real-time biologically meaningful HSNN prostheses.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Position Control of Robotic Manipulators
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper we offer the position controller of robotic manipulators subject to finite-time convergence. The feedback controller is an extension of the traditional PD control of robotic manipulators. Furthermore, we introduce a continuous function to smooth the control law and the proposed controller is absolutely continuous. The numerical simulation results carried out for a two-link robotic manipulator illustrate performance of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: A Method of Shear Line Automatic Identification on High-precision Numerical Data
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Shear line identification and analysis is important in weather forecasting based on numerical data. An algorithm of shear line automatic identification from numerical data is proposed in this paper. First, a statistical feature was developed preliminarily filter regional wind data to obtain interesting area including shear band areas, then it was processed with two median filters. Second, the shear mathematical mode was constructed to cut out the local areas related to the shear type. The distance and location between wind areas were calculated to collect the point set of the shear band. Third, the DBScan clustering algorithm was used to cluster those provisional shear bands. Forth, the final shear line was selected according to the angle of shear line type. Experimental results shown that the proposed algorithm is effective by calculating the indexes of POD, FAR and CSI in identifying cold shear and warm shear from the numerical wind data in May 2015.

articleTitle: A terminal guidance law basing on variable universe adaptive fuzzy approach for intercepting maneuvering space targets
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: A terminal guidance law basing on variable universe direct adaptive fuzzy approach is developed for intercepting maneuvering space targets. By defining the target acceleration as an unknown disturbance, the adaptive laws on a Lyapunov function are developed to adjust the parameters of the fuzzy rules to guarantee the stability of the system. The guidance law not only keeps the angle rate of line of sight between interception and target converging to zero, but also guarantees intercepting all kinds of maneuvering targets. The simulation results show that by introducing the guidance law will achieve the almost zero miss distance and the robustness.

articleTitle: A Fractional-order PIλDμ Controller Based on the Biggest Stability Region for PMSM
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In industrial applications, conventional integer PID controllers are widely used in surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) control systems. However, the conventional integer PID controller can not be robust against parameter variation. In order to solve the problem, the conventional integer PID controller is replaced by the fractional-order PIλDμ controller. The size of stability region in terms of parameter space P(k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>, k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub>, k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sub>, λ, μ) has a considerable effect on the robustness of field-oriented control (FOC). With this in mind, based on the stability boundary locus method, the biggest stability region determination strategy of fractional-order PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">μ</sup> controller for speed-loop control is proposed in this paper by checking the parameter orders λ and μ which correspond to the biggest stability region. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is confirmed by simulations. Results show that a higher robustness can be achieved when parameters are perturbed, the dynamic performance can be enhanced significantly as well.

articleTitle: Analysis for Resonance Characteristics of Magnetic Resonant Coupling Wireless Power Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In view of unclear understanding of the resonance characteristics of a magnetic resonant coupling based wireless power transmission system, the definition of resonance frequency, resonance parameter characteristics, and shape of power-frequency response curve are discussed in this paper based on a mutual inductance coupling circuit model. The main conclusions drawn in this paper are as follows: relative to the frequency corresponding to system transmission efficiency peak point, defining the operating frequency under the peak power transmission condition as the resonance frequency is more reasonable; under resonance conditions, the system equivalent reactance is zero; in the overcoupling zone, when the sum of the operating frequency values corresponding to two peak powers is greater than twice as much as the loosely coupled resonance frequency, the main resonance frequency is the frequency corresponding to the first peak power; otherwise, the second. Simulation analysis and experimental results verify the conclusions in this paper.

articleTitle: Metropolitan France Population Projection Based on Weights-and-Structure-Determination Neuronet
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: As one of the most important factors of human development, population always attracts the attention of many researchers. Accurate population projection can help the government make more correct and more effective decisions. Among many methods of population projection, the artificial neuronet method not only generates simple and reliable models but also is widely used. In this paper, we use the weights-and-structure-determination (WASD) neuronet to make a projection for Metropolitan France population. Due to the unevenness of the historical population data, we use the cubic spline method to preprocess data. Then, we use the twice-pruning algorithm to construct the WASD neuronet to balance the learning ability and the projection ability. After analyzing the future population projection results of Metropolitan France, we draw a conclusion that the population of Metropolitan France is most likely to rise in the next 20 years.

articleTitle: Bifurcation analysis of fractional-order gene regulatory system with delay
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper studies the bifurcation of the three variables fractional gene regulatory networks(FGRNs), mainly regards the time delay as the bifurcation point. The lowest order bifurcation point is obtained. The two different states around the bifurcation point are derived, and the attribute of bifurcation is studied too. Finally, some numerical simulation examples are provided to verify the effectiveness and the advantage of the proposed bifurcation criterion.

articleTitle: Distributed Control of A Class of Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems with Switching Topologies
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper presents a cyclic-small-gain approach to distributed control of non linear multi-agent systems with switching topologies for output agreement. Each agent is assumed to be in the strict output-feedback form. By introducing a new dynamic mechanism, a dynamic compensator, a local state-observer and a state transformation, the multi-agent system is transformed into a dynamic network having switching topology and consisting of input-to-output stable and unboundedness observable subsystems. The output agreement is verified to be realized by guaranteeing the stability of the dynamic network with the help of the cyclic-small-gain theorem.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Disturbance Observer Based Adaptive Dynamic Surface Control for Full Actuated Ship Trajectory Tracking
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: For the trajectory tracking control problem of three degrees of freedom full actuated ships, a disturbance observer-baded robust adaptive dynamic surface control scheme is proposed. The disturbance observer is constructed to acquire the signal of the unknown external environmental disturbance for compensating with the form of feedforward. In addition, a adaptive law with the leakage terms of ı-modification is designed to estimate the bounds of observation errors. The dynamic surface control (DSC) technique is introduced to remove the need of the derivation operation for the virtual control vector, which makes the proposed control scheme is easy to implement in engineering practice. Under the proposed control scheme, all the signal of trajectory tracking close-loop control system are bounded. Simulation results and comparisons with standard DSC method illustrate the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Static Positioning Performance Evaluation Method of GBAS Based on Interval Counting
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Ground-based Augmentation system (GBAS) is a new navigation and positioning system based on differential positioning technology. Civil aircraft can use GBAS to achieve high-accuracy, high-reliability approach landing. Positioning accuracy is one of the key factors to judge the performance of GBAS navigation services. In this paper, we analyse the fundamental principle of GBAS differential positioning and apply self-program software and measured data to evaluate the positioning error of self-developed GBAS platform. But in the case of large sample data, the calculation of circular error would cost a great deal of time and internal storage. In order to solve the above problems, we propose a fast calculation method of circular error based on interval counting which can improve the efficiency of positioning performance evaluation. The experimental results show that this method can evaluate the static positioning performance of GBAS quickly and effectively without lossing the evaluation precision.

articleTitle: Set-Membership Event-Based Node-to-Node Consensus of Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, we study the set-membership node-to-node consensus problem for nonlinear discrete-time multi-agent systems with bounded noises. A set-membership consensus protocol, which is based on a new event-triggered communication mechanism, is presented. The scheduling of sensor information between the leaders' layer and the followers' layer is ruled by the event-triggered mechanism. Sufficient conditions are derived for the existence of the node-to-node consensus protocol and the parameters of the desired consensus protocol are obtained by solving a set of recursive linear matrix inequalities. Finally, two examples are utilized to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed node-to-node consensus protocol.

articleTitle: Study on Conductivity Distribution of Human Lung
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This study is aim to analyze the conductivity data of cancerous tissues and normal tissues of human lung, establish the conductivity distribution model and investigate the conductivity characteristics of cancerous and normal tissues which provide the basic theory and reference data for medical research and clinical diagnosis of lung cancer. The lung cancer tissues and the normal tissues around the tumor from lung cancer patients were taken as specimens. Then the impedances of specimens were measured by impedance analyzer under the temperature and humidity at expected values. After calculating the conductivities of the specimens and determining the locations of the tumors, the conductivity distribution models of human cancerous and normal lung were established. As the excitation current frequency increases, the conductivity of the cancerous or normal tissue rises. And the conductivities of cancerous tissues are higher than that of normal tissues. For cancerous lung model, the conductivity of the left lung is higher than that of the right lung. While the contrary for normal lung model. There is a trend that the conductivity decreases from the upper lobe to the lower lobe of lung model.

articleTitle: Application of Adaptive Kalman Filter in Velocity Measurement of Magnetic Levitation Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In order to effectively suppress the measurement noise on the speed of medium and low speed magnetic levitation interference is too large, a method using adaptive Kalman filter algorithm of low speed magnetic levitation jamming filter. This algorithm improves the accuracy of traditional Kalman by calculating the maximum likelihood estimation of the variance of the new interest theory and introducing it into the Kalman filtering algorithm. The experimental results show that compared with traditional Kalman filtering and traditional filtering methods, it has better filtering effect and is easy to be applied in engineering practice.

articleTitle: An improved CRC calibration in power communication
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of check miss rate in CRC check in power communication, this paper adopts the method of parallel packet check to select the optimal number of packets while reducing the missed check rate of CRC check. Firstly, by analyzing the CRC calibration algorithm, the error detection ability of the algorithm is obtained, and then, through the method of mathematical proofs, a new method to reduce the transmission of BER is proposed; Secondly, because the end uses a parallel check circuit, this circuit introduces a new problem while reducing the check time. Although using parallel packet verification can reduce time, it also consumes more hardware resources at the same time, and high requirements may lead to new interference and error detection problems; Thirdly, through experimental analysis, the optimal number of subgroups is selected.

articleTitle: Adaptive Critic H∞ Control of Nonlinear Systems With Disturbance and Input Constraints
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: For a class of discrete-time nonlinear systems with known internal dynamics, one of the problems worth discussing is H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> formula, which could be used to attenuate the influence of disturbance effectively. To deal with the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> control problem for nonlinear systems with disturbance and input constraints, we need to get the solution of the corresponding Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs (HJI) equation that is difficult to solve by mathematical analysis. This paper provides an online adaptive critic learning algorithm to obtain the approximate Nash equilibrium solutions of the two-player zero-sum game, which has the close connection with H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> control. Meanwhile, a non-quadratic performance functional is introduced to handle the constrained problem. In order to implement the algorithm, a framework based on actor-critic-disturbance structure is designed and three neural networks are constructed. Finally, via simulation study, the applicability of the proposed scheme is verified.

articleTitle: Robust Real-Time Object Tracking using Tiered Templates
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Object tracking has been an important topic in the field of computer vision. This paper proposes a robust method of tracking a moving object continuously in real-time without prior information and learning. The key strategies involved in this novel method are: combining intensity template matching with colour histogram model to increase tracking robustness, employing a three-tier system to store templates, applying update and tracking policies for template management. Experiment results have shown that the proposed method achieved the highest tracking accuracy among existing methods from various benchmark videos.

articleTitle: Coverage control for heterogeneous mobile sensor networks with unidirectional locomotion on a circle
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper addresses the coverage control problem for a network of heterogeneous mobile sensors which are constrained to move forward. The goal of the problem is to minimize a coverage cost function which is defined as the largest arrival time from the mobile sensor network to the points on a circle. Low gain feedback is applied to design a distributed control law for each sensor with first-order dynamics and the upper bound of the low gain is provided. It is proved that the sensors can be driven to the optimal configuration such that the coverage cost function is minimized. The sensors' order is preserved during the coverage task. The effectiveness of the proposed control law is verified by simulations.

articleTitle: A dynamic 3D trajectory optimization of continuous descent approach for low fuel consumption
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Compared with traditional step-down approach procedure, continuous descent approach (CDA) can save fuel and reduce noise. This article presents a method to generate dynamic CDA trajectories in three-dimensional space with optimal fuel consumption. The optimization range of this method is from the IAF to the FAF. When the aircraft enters the terminal area, it can dynamically generate a lateral path according to the real-time status of the aircraft and the obstacle information. Then, it generates the optimal fuel consumption CDA vertical profile. At last, it establishes the available 3D trajectory. This trajectory can be real-time to ensure the safety of the aircraft, and only need near idle thrust which can save fuel. Simulations are performed to show the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Preliminary found of Lung cancer information contained in ECG
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Over the past decades, the incidence and mortality of lung cancer have increased rapidly, especially for male, which are higher than those of other malignant tumors. At present, radionuclide, fiberoptic bronchoscopy, X-ray, pulmonary biopsy and sputum exfoliative cytology are the most common diagnostic methods for lung cancer. However, these methods are high cost and cannot be used for long periods of time. At the same time, they bring patients suffering. In this paper, Electrocardiograms (ECGs) were analyzed to explore the contained information of lungs. By comparing ECG sampling data between four kinds of typical lung cancer patients and healthy people, a conclusion was made that the voltage of the precordial lead of the cancer patients is higher than the healthy person, which can be used in the preliminary diagnosis of lung cancer.

articleTitle: A Hardware Platform for Wireless Structural Health Monitoring Based on Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, a novel hardware platform is proposed for wireless structural health monitoring in real time based on compressed sensing. The platform consists of a three-axis accelerometer sensor, a high-precision multi-channel analog-to-digital converter, a wireless communication module and a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) chip. Firstly, the three-axis acceleration signal of the structure are sampled and compressed simultaneously using a compressed sensing encoder. Secondly, the compressed data are transmitted to a fusion center via a wireless link. Finally, the acceleration signal are reconstructed and the structural health situation is evaluated. Experimental results show that the proposed framework has excellent signal measurement performance, thus making it practical for long term wireless structural health monitoring applications.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic Based Scheduling for 2-keto-L-gulonic Acid Production
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In 2-keto-L-gulonic acid (2-KGA) industrial fermentation workshop, L-sorbose resource is allocated evenly among batches and the batch-to-batch variations are not considered. A fuzzy logic based scheduling approach is presented to maximize the profit of 2-KGA fermentation processes by improving L-sorbose resource allocation. The profit-making ability of each 2-KGA batch is evaluated by the online classification of the profit function. The batches having great profit-making potential will be assigned more L-sorbose, and its cultivation period is estimated with fuzzy logic method. The profit increment from re-allocating L-sorbose is then calculated by the implementation of pseudo-on-line scheduling with the industrial data of 2-KGA cultivations. The results show that total profit increase is 4.82% when compared with the traditional operation for the workshop.

articleTitle: Guaranteed Cost Load-Following Control of Nuclear Reactor Power Based on T - S Fuzzy Model
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The load-following control is a very important technology to ensure the safe and stable operation of nuclear reactors. In this paper, a guaranteed cost control system based on T-S fuzzy model is presented to improve the nuclear reactor load-following capability. First, the nonlinear reactor core model is transformed into a T-S fuzzy model based on the division of five relative initial power points. Then, combining the Lyapunov stability theory, a state observer is introduced to solve the problem that some state variables cannot be measured. Finally, a guaranteed cost load-following controller is obtained by solving linear matrix inequalities. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed controller can effectively complete the load-following control and the coolant temperature also complies with the operating requirements.

articleTitle: Sliding mode control of a large-scale wind turbine by considering partial loads
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: During the maximum power point tracking stage of the wind turbine, we not only need to design the controller to ensure that as much wind energy as possible is extracted. During this process, it is also necessary to reduce the influence of mechanical load on the wind turbine. However, most articles ignored the effect of mechanical loads on wind turbines in order to pursue greater wind energy efficiency. Therefore, the balance between the extraction efficiency of wind energy and the reduction of load is a key issue. In this paper, we design a new type of large-scale wind turbine sliding-mode controller based on the load, which ensures that under the premise of power tracking, the mechanical load is greatly reduced. Then, in FAST, we compare the advantages of the modified method with other existing methods.

articleTitle: Design of Course Controller for Atmospheric Diving Suit (ADS) based on Adaptive Sliding Mode Control with Extended State Observer (ESO)
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: During the underwater directional operation of the atmospheric diving suit (ADS), the ADS system encounters problems caused by external disturbances, parameter uncertainties and time-varying terms. To solve these problems, an ADS course controller is proposed based on adaptive sliding mode control with extended state observer (ESO). The ESO can effectively estimate the disturbances in order to realize compensation, while the adaptive sliding mode controller has good robustness and enables further compensation. The designing process of the ADS course controller is described in detail in this paper. The system stability and convergence are proved using the Lyapunov stability criterion and are testified through simulation experiments. Simulation results show that the proposed controller has good robustness and achieves satisfying performance in ADS course control.

articleTitle: Optimal control for multi-agent systems persistent monitoring with limited energy
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper studies the optimal control for persistent monitoring, which aims to let multiple agents periodically patrol the mission domain along a given closed path to drive the uncertainty of all targets to zero. A necessary and sufficient condition that drives non-linear cumulative function to zero is derived. In this condition, different speed controllers are further designed by solving a linear program problem (LP). And a method that maximizes the working hours of the multiple agents with limited energy is developed by a LP. Finally, simulation results evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed optimal control law.

articleTitle: A novel image encryption algorithm based on compressed sensing theory and hyper-chaotic system
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: A novel image encryption algorithm is proposed based on compressed sensing theory and hyper-chaotic system. This algorithm can improve the flaws of traditional image encryption methods such as low safety, strong information correction and high cost of storage and transmission. In this algorithm, we combine compressed sensing with scrambling and diffusion scheme through hyper-chaotic Lorenz map. In the process of compressed sensing, the measurement matrix is designed by chaotic sequence and the discrete wavelet transform matrix is selected as sparse matrix. Then plaintext-related scrambling and diffusion algorithm is used to further strengthen the ability of the encryption algorithm to resist differential attacks. Simulation results and security analyses verify that the algorithm has the advantages of strong confidentiality, large key space and high reconstruction accuracy.

articleTitle: A Robust Framework for Cell Orientation Control by Using a Robot-Aided Optical Tweezers Manipulation System
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Biological cells orientation control is a vital important technique involved in cell surgery research. Currently, most the reported approaches to the cell orientation control are performed manually, with low precision and repeatability. Optical tweezers have exhibited significant advantages in manipulation of single cells, including cell orientation control. Some reported approaches for cell orientation control have adopted a simple PID type control, neglecting the model uncertainties and external disturbances. In this paper, a robust control strategy is presented to achieve orientation control of single cells with enhanced manipulation reliability and robustness. The stability and robustness of the closed-loop control systemis analyzed based on a direct Lyapunov method. Both simulation and experimental results are shown to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Design of Test System for Micro-power Communication Module of Smart Meter
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: this paper has carried on the thorough analysis to the test system of the micro-power communication module, and explained the meaning of the automation test of the communication module, as well as constructed the overall frame and workflow of the automation test. The proposed automatic test process can realize the appearance check of the communication module through an image recognition technology, besides, it can also complete the protocol conformance test. Meanwhile, this paper also describes the application and design of electromagnetic anechoic chamber for micro-power communication module test. The design proposed in this paper provides technical support for the efficient verification of micro-power communication module.

articleTitle: An Improved Method of Gray-Code with Binocular Vision for Workpiece 3D Measurement
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In order to achieve the requirement of 3D shape measurement for workpiece, such as spray painting, welding and grinding, an improved binocular vision 3D measurement method based on Gray code structured light is proposed. First, the calibration parameters of the binocular camera are calibrated off-line, and then the black-and-white inverse reprojection method is applied to obtain the clear gray code boundary for the traditional structured light boundary fuzzy problem. Then, a fast region block search strategy is proposed for stereo matching to get disparity map. Finally, the bilinear interpolation method is applied to fill the vacancy of disparity map to solve the problem of binocular blind angle measurement, thus obtaining full depth information. The experimental results show that this method can quickly achieve high-precision three-dimensional reconstruction of the workpiece, especially for non-textured and weakly-textured workpiece can obtain better results, to meet the requirement of 3D measurement in the industrial environment.

articleTitle: Using Gaze Patterns to Infer Human Intention for Human-Robot Interaction
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The ability of an service robot to analyze and infer user’s intent is essential to provide friendly service for users. This paper describes a novel and practical gaze-based intention inference framework. Existing frameworks primarily establish the relationship of gaze points with objects, which is lack of mining of implicit information contained in eye gaze and prediction of human’s intention. In our framework, the user’s gaze is tracked using a model-based method and analyzed using two levels of unsupervised learning algorithms. The first level is that clustering gaze points and matching them with objects to enable the robot to understand semantic information of gazed objects. The second level is correlation analysis of gazed objects with behaviors, according to the user’s daily living habits and gazed objects, the service robot can speculate concrete and proper behaviors from implicit user’s intent.
