The advantage of this framework is that more effective and intuitive human-robot interaction can be realized only with a consumer level depth sensor (Kinect) and a normal laptop, even for the disabled person.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Method of the Reference Field for Electrical Impedance Tomography
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Detecting the components in a vessel has been a crucial study in the field of industry, and Electrical impedance tomography (EIT) has been developed to solve this issue in a fast and non-invasive way. As the components move, the conductivity varies rapidly, and the background conductivity should be adjusted to adapt to this change. Now that the real-time measurements, the shape of the boundary and the electrode distribution are available, voltages of a basic reference field (uniform field) can be calculated, and the reference field can be estimated based on the real-time measurements. A fast estimation method based on two criteria is proposed. A set of simulations were made to test the effectiveness of the adjusted reference measurements. For models under various background and object conductivity, the voltages of the reference field were estimated based on a basic reference field, and the conductivity distribution of each model was reconstructed. Simulation results lead to the conclusion that the estimation methods are effective in adjusting voltages of reference field, and one of the criteria can even improve the image quality.

articleTitle: Application of Fisher-PCA in Fault Diagnosis of TE Process
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: For the current plant big data, high-dimensional production environment, and the need for quick diagnosis of plant failures, this paper proposes an improved Fisher-PCA dimension reduction method for quick fault diagnosis of the entire system. This method is based on principal component analysis. Using the advantage of PCA dimensionality reduction on data loss, the Fisher criteria function is rapidly diagnosed in high-dimensional data. This method is applied to the TE process which is a real simulation of the strong coupling chemical production process. Simulation experiments show that this method can effectively distinguish the high-dimensional coupled fault data and normal data, and the method is practical and effective.

articleTitle: Navigation Scheme of Mobile Robots and Its Application at Airport Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Intelligent mobile robots have been widely used in the fields of manufacturing, service, military, interstellar detection and so on. Navigation is an important problem if intelligent mobile robots want to realize autonomous control. This paper proposes a novel navigation scheme for robots moving at airport, which provide special services for VIP customers, such as going for checking, porterage and so on. The integration way of A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> method and artificial potential way is presented to achieve dynamic path planning of the robots with lots of moving obstacles. This method can be used to solve the bottleneck that the artificial potential field method is easy to fall into local minimum. The posture is obtained by using UWB (Ultra-Wide Band), and the accuracy can reach 10cm or less, and the distance up to about 500 meters. The experiment shows the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Large Margin Distribution Machine for Imbalanced Data Classification
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The imbalanced data classification problem is common in many real-world supervised learning tasks, and always leads to the lower class-prediction accuracy of the minority class. In this paper, a modified large margin distribution machine is proposed by adjust the kernel matrix based on the distribution of the data near the class boundary, to improve the class-prediction accuracy. Through theoretical analysis backed by empirical study, it shows that the proposed algorithm in this paper works effectively on several UCI datasets.

articleTitle: Design, Analysis and Experiments of Bionic Hexapod Robot with Multilayer C-shape Legs for Unstructured Terrain
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Wheeled robot seems to be the best vehicles, however it can't pass unstructured terrain; tracked robot has the ability to go through unstructured terrain, but it has the disadvantages of heavy mass and poor speed. In order to conquer those shortcomings, this paper proposes a novel hexapod robot, which can move fast and even climb stairs easily. Firstly, the design of hexapod robot is explained with our unique multilayer C-shape legs, which are developed to effectively reduce stress concentration problem on leg. Secondly, a complete dynamic analysis is made to prove the feasibility of structure and algorithm. Thirdly, an intelligence control algorithm is developed to improve the robustness. Moreover, the simulation and physical experiment results are given to verify the proposed design and algorithm.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Direct Electro-pneumatic Brake Based on Model and Data-driven
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: According to dynamic features of strong coupling, non-linearity and uncertainty for direct electro-pneumatic brake, a fault diagnosis architecture based on model and data-driven is proposed to detect and isolate dynamic faults of solenoid valves and pressure sensors. Firstly, a sequentially structured fault diagnosis scheme is designed. Secondly, the state of the solenoid valves can be characterized after analyzing the drive current of solenoid valves and the fault diagnosis of solenoid valves is realized by using wavelet packet decomposition to extract the feature and the back propagation (BP) neural network to classify the fault type. Thirdly, the charging and discharging process of direct electro-pneumatic brake is described with analysis model, which can generate system residual. So the fault diagnosis for the sensor can be achieved. Finally, a test platform is designed and a series of experiments are conducted. Experiment results show that the fault diagnosis architecture and technologies designed in this paper can make fast and reliable diagnosis.

articleTitle: Closed-Loop Control of Trajectory Tracking a Microparticle through an Electromagnetic Manipulation System
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: With the advantages of minimally invasive feature and insensitivity to biological substances, magnetic force-based manipulation has exhibited great biomedical application potential, where microparticles are driven to follow desired trajectories. This study proposes a closed-loop control approach for automated manipulation of magnetic microbeads using a self-made electromagnetic coil system. A visual-based closed-loop controller that incorporates the concept of input-to-state stability is developed, which enables the bead to follow the desired trajectory successfully, while maintaining the tracking error within a local area under model uncertainties and environmental disturbances. A high-gain observer is further designed to estimate the bead velocity, which solves the difficulty of measuring the bead velocity via visual feedback. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method could be effective.

articleTitle: Energy Management Strategy of Wind-Photovoltaic-Storage Micro-grid System Considering Battery Life
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: With the rapid growth of the proportion of new energy power, wind-photovoltaic (PV)-storage complementary power generation has become an important part of China's power provision. An energy management strategy for the wind-PV-storage micro-grid (MG) system is presented in this paper. By considering the system operation cost, battery life loss cost and environment cost of purchasing power, an economic dispatch model is established. Taking the lowest integrated cost of power generation as the goal, considering the constraints of output force and safety performance, the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is used to generate the parameters of the energy management strategy for optimizing power scheduling. Under different weather conditions, the better effectiveness of the proposed strategy is verified by comparing the simulation results of the proposed strategy with those of the conventional strategy. Based on the example data, the influence of the depth and frequency of battery charge and discharge on the battery's life is discussed, and the battery life is longer under the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Analysis and Simulation of VSC in Superconducting Magnetic Energy System
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Aiming at the power conditioning system (PCS) in the superconducting magnetic energy system (SMES) based on voltage source converter (VSC), this paper gave the main circuit structure of PCS in the SMES based on the VSC and chopper, as well as the low-frequency mathematical model of PCS which is expressed in the functions of duty ratio. The non-linear transformation was used to linearize state equations to realize the decoupled control between active power, reactive power and DC voltage. The simulated results in Simulink of Matlab showed that the designed PCS has perfect performance in tracing power orders in the form of step and sine waves with strong anti-jamming ability for voltage at DC side.

articleTitle: Event-triggered control of switched linear systems: the elementary time unit approach
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, a novel event-triggered control is proposed for switched linear systems based on the elementary time unit (ETU) approach. The interval of the active subsystems is consisted of some segments called ETUs. The time-scheduled Lyapunov function is used and the switching signal with mode-dependent average dwell time (MDADT) is designed to guarantee the exponential stability of switched linear systems with unstable modes. Furthermore, we design an event-triggered mechanism involving ETU, which excludes the possibility of continuous triggering, thus Zeno behavior is avoid naturally. The number of triggering can also be reduced. Finally, a numerical example is provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Density Peak Clustering Algorithm Based on Optimal Density Radius
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The density peaks clustering (DPC) algorithm is one of the most important progress in recent clustering algorithms, which needs neither any iterative process nor more parameters, and thus takes advantages over most existing clustering algorithms. But the density radius is an uncertain parameter in DPC, and its different values may lead to very different clustering results. This problem greatly limits its applicable range. In this paper, an efficient method is proposed to determine the density radius. The core idea is that an optimal density radius must maximize the density differences of all samples. Consequently, the uncertain parameter in the DPC algorithm is optimally determined. The experimental results of a set of real data sets with different structures show that the improved DPC algorithm has higher clustering accuracy than the original DPC algorithm, and essentially has more robust clustering results.

articleTitle: Characterizing Complexity of Electroencephalograms in Alzheimer's Disease at Multiple Temporal Scales
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Entropy is a widely-used feature and a basic framework for electroencephalogram (EEG) analyses. Their corresponding multiscale methods were recently developed, adopting multiple time scales for entropy estimation. In this paper, towards Alzheimer's disease (AD) EEG recordings, we employed weighted-permutation entropy combining multiscale analysis, so that multiscale complexity information could be exposed across different scale factors. Our experiment and off-line analyses results confirmed that multiscale weighted-permutation entropy (MWPE) method could distinguish AD pattern and control pattern in terms of the evolution trend of MWPE profiles. The consistency of 16 channels were broken in AD brain. The entropy topographic distribution in AD patients distinctly differed from healthy subjects at large-scale.

articleTitle: Bounds on Delay Margin for Consensus of General Second-Order Multi-Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper studies the delay margin and its bounds for second-order multi-agent systems to achieve robust consensus with respect to uncertain delays varying within a range. The issue under investigation dwells on the question: What is the largest delay range within which a distributed control protocol is able to achieve and maintain the consensus? We consider second-order agents with real unstable poles communicating over an undirected network topology, and derive bounds on the delay margin. The results show that for a strictly unstable second-order multi-agent system, its consensuability robustness depends on the pole locations of the agents, as well as on the eigen-ratio of the network graph.

articleTitle: The Novel Nonlinear Dynamics and Performance in Switch Circuit with Memristor Load Applied
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Memristor has always been performed in chaotic systems to stimulate new chaotic features, but it has never applied in a switch circuit like a boost converter. In this paper, the low power boost converter with memristor load is investigated. It may give a new idea of application for memristor. The constitutive relation of the memristor is built to explore new dynamical behaviors. It is quite different with traditional boost converter, because the step-up ratio is mainly decided by the memristor's parameters and inductor current. Meanwhile, mathematical modeling is brought for a further comprehension. Phase portraits show distinguishing characters. Power spectrum helps to distinguish the periodic and chaotic behaviors. Numerical simulation and circuit experiments make a good comparison and verification.

articleTitle: Leader-following Consensus of Heterogeneous Bilinear Multi-agent Systems via Bounded Input
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, leader-following consensus problem of heterogeneous bilinear multi-agent systems subject to saturation characteristics of actuators is investigated. A new distributed consensus bounded input control law is proposed depending on information interchange with the adjacent agents and the dynamic parameter of follower agent itself. Leader-following consensus is achieved under the bounded control laws under the undirected communication topology graph, which is connected and there is a agent as leader in the multi-agent systems. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed theorem is verified by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Model Predictive Control for a Multi-reach Open-channel System
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: In this paper, application of a hierarchical predictive controller in an accurate model of an open-channel system is presented. The system is based on the linearized Saint-Venant equations, a set of partial differential equations, which describes the hydraulic dynamics of canals and implemented by Simulation of Irrigation Canals (SIC). The hierarchical predictive controller consists of two layers. The lower layer is made up of numerous local proportional integral differential controllers (PID controllers) in order to regulate each gate rapidly, while the higher layer is made up of a centralized model predictive controller that modifies the setpoints of local PID controllers according to the global water level, flow and gate opening information when the control period arrives. This scheme uses linearized Saint-Venant (S-v) equations as the predict model. Hence, a more accurate method that predicts future water level is expected to realized. Therefore, it is possible to more accurately predict the future water level.

articleTitle: Adaptive Local Data Density for Clustering Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Density is a key statistical quantity and is widely applied in clustering analysis, but various existing approaches to computing data density have to be specified by prior information or user's experiences. Moreover, these data densities are computed by global rather than local density threshold, while any cluster consists of a group of locally high-density data in fact. Once data density is incorrectly determined, the related clustering results are guaranteed no longer. In this paper, we propose an adaptive and local method to compute data density by a simple bisecting process. All data samples in a dataset are continually bisected according to their k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) distances and adaptively grouped by their competing relations. Consequently, the computed data density perfectly is unsupervised without prior information or user's experiences. Moreover, it is a local notation and consistent in the clustering process. Experimental results validate the proposed method and its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Network Traffic Classification Based on AR-ELM Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Accurate network traffic classification is of fundamental importance to network traffic measurement and analysis. Machine learning based approaches takes use of various characteristics instead of only depending on port numbers and protocol details. This paper proposes a traffic classification approach based on extreme learning machine(ELM), in which a rough set is before ELM algorithms applied in classification. Comparing to the huge time-consuming, low accuracy rates and inefficient capability of the classification of the conventional algorithms, an extreme learning machine proposed for classification model. Comparing hierarchical extreme learning machine (H-ELM) to AR-ELM, the results of experiment shows that AR-ELM algorithm can be used in classification effectively and the classification based on ELM model has many advantages like quite fast training speed and low error rate. H-ELM improves the overall learning performance by removing redundancy of the original inputs with compact features. The proposed AR-ELM conducts the classification in combination with the advantages of both ELM and H-ELM.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis for Machine Tool Energy Approach based on Extended Stochastic Petri Nets
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: High energy efficiency has become a critical requirement of companies. An effective energy consumption assessment model for machine tool is presented based on the Extended Stochastic Petri Nets and the analysis approach is also proposed using behavior expression. The energy consumption states and machine tool modes are unified the places of model, and the change information of energy is added to the transitions of model. An actual example, a turn machine tool production processes is addressed and the power and cycle time indicators are discussed.

articleTitle: Fast Moving Human Detection using Depth Information
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: A novel approach to real-time moving human detection using depth information is proposed in this paper. The captured depth images are used to construct a codebook-based foreground-background segmentation module. Then, Laplace operator is applied to extract the foreground object edges for calculating contour length. Meanwhile, a ground coordinate system (GCS) is established to measure the height of objects in foreground. Moving human is finally detected by synthesizing contour length and height information. The proposed approach can detect and label moving human in real-time without any initialization or training procedure, and can detect multiple people with different poses and solve occlusion problem. With the comparison of other algorithms in three different datasets, the proposed method can achieve more accurate and robust detection results.

articleTitle: The Characteristics Evaluation of a VR Simulator-based Catheter Training System
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: So many patients get benefit from endovascular surgeries because of the miniature wound and fast healing, but how to achieve the goal of endovascular surgeries need the doctor to master their skill and ensure that not to made damage to the patients. A training system which cooperated with VR simulator system is in desperately indeed. The VR simulator could simulate the position and form of the catheter. A controlling device also could make the novice surgeons understand the insertion and rotation to the catheter. At the same time, the feedback system could also provides advantages for training. The performance is evaluated from the displacement in VR system and force feedback from haptic device. The results demonstrate that the enhance after training is about 38%. Based on the result we could announced that our VR simulator based catheter training system provide the a effective way for those surgeons under training

articleTitle: Characteristics Evaluation of the Vascular Interventional Surgery Robot in the Simulated Vascular Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper proposed a novel master-slave catheter robotic system with force feedback for Vascular Interventional Surgery (VIS). The master side of the doctor feedback force was achieved by the principle of electromagnetic induction. It used an incremental photoelectric encoder to detect axial and radial motion information of the master side. Load cell was used to detect force information on the slave side. Besides, we also set up a circulating peristaltic pump to simulate the fluid environment. According to the blood flow velocity parameters of the human body, we set the velocity of the peristaltic pump, and the force feedback experiment and the master-slave tracking experiment were completed. Experimental results showed that with the increase of the fluid velocity, the tracking error and force feedback error of the master side and the slave side would increase obviously, but the errors were within the allowable range, which indicated that the catheter robotic system has good force feedback and motion tracking performance.

articleTitle: Novel hybrid intelligent evolutionary algorithm for dynamic optimization problems
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Dynamic optimization is used to make a performance index optimal by controlling operational variables in dynamic model. Intelligent algorithms based on intelligent evolutionary become popular for solving dynamic optimization problems. The general methods based on the gradient method cannot handle the cases that the gradients are not available. For solving this problem, a hybrid genetic algorithm combining the differential evolution and artificial fish swarm algorithm is proposed. The proposed algorithm is successfully tested on several cases and the results show the feasibility and efficiency of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Stability of Lur’e-type Discrete-time Reset Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper studies the stability of lur'e-type discrete-time reset control systems. Sufficient conditions for global asymptotic stability of lur'e-type discrete-time descriptor systems for both partial and full state reset cases have been obtained via the generalized Lyapunov function and linear matrix inequality(LMI) theories. An illustrative example is provided to show the application of the proposed results.

articleTitle: A Primary and Secondary Feature Priority Classification Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Decision tree has been proved to be an effective classifier. Inspired by the decision tree, a single-feature classification is analyzed and then a primary and secondary feature priority (PSFP) classification algorithm is proposed. To examine the performance of our proposed classification algorithm, two different tests were carried out: slow cortical potential (SCP) signal classification and Chinese liquor recognition. Experimental results reveal that for the SCP signal classification using the BCI competition II dataset Ia, an accuracy of 95.9% is obtained through the PSFP algorithm, better than that (92.30%) of the state-of-the-art method (V-ELM). When applied the PSFP algorithm to the Chinese liquor recognition, a classification accuracy of 100% is obtained, which further verified the performance of our proposed PSFP classification algorithm.

articleTitle: Determining the optimal stimulus waveforms of deep brain stimulation based on support vector machine
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) has been proven to be an effective treatment for neurological diseases. Currently, selection of stimulation parameters of DBS is mainly relying on the trial and error method which is time-consuming and cannot obtain an optimal treatment performance. Thus, determining parameters of DBS based on the real time states of the brain is appealing. In this paper, a method for choosing parameters of DBS according to firing rates of neurons based on support vector machine is presented. Firstly, the effects of different DBS parameters on the firing rates of neurons are analyzed, then the mapping relationships from DBS inputs to the firing rates of neurons are classified by support vector machine (SVM). Thus the optimal stimulus waveforms of DBS which could result in expected firing rates of neurons can be searched based on the mapping relationships.

articleTitle: Laguerre Functions Based Model Predictive Control for Constrained Servo Turntable
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: We consider a single-axis servo turntable with input voltage limit which is typical DC-motor controller design, as a discrete-time, finite-horizon optimal control problem with constraints. We utilize a set of discrete functions with orthogonality based on Laguerre polynomials into the process of controller design. The control sequence can be calculated online repeatedly to replace the offline calculation of optimal control problem with constraints. An augmented state-space model is derived with no requirement of observer and the asymptotic stability can be guaranteed. Simulation and comparison results for tracking the angular position set-points of the servo turntable are given. The high performance of model predictive control demonstrates the practicality of the proposed method into engineering applications.

articleTitle: Mobile Robot Path Planning in Complicated Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: The function of potential field in the traditional artificial potential field method only contains the position distance information, it can only deal with the path planning in static environment. By modifying the potential field, the velocity and acceleration information are introduced into the function of potential field to make the robot can avoid dynamic obstacle. In addition, taking into account the large number of static and dynamic obstacles in complex environment, A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> algorithm is used to obtain the global sub-target points to guide the robot path planning. Simulation results show that the improved artificial potential field method can not only avoid dynamic obstacles but also get the optimized path.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Current Sharing Strategy for Energy Storage Urban Rails Using Extremum Seeking
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Cooperative proportional-integral (PI) has been a popular current sharing method in many industrial applications for its simplicity and reliability. However, since cooperative PI control is typically implemented in a decentralized way, the parameter tuning of cooperative PI controllers is a time-consuming task when the number of controllers is large. In this paper, we propose an improved cooperative PI controller with adaptive parameter tuning using extremum seeking algorithm. It is shown that parameters of the cooperative PI controllers can be tuned adaptively by extremum seeking algorithm to achieve the precise current sharing among converters. Simulation results are provided to verify the feasibility of the proposed design.

articleTitle: A Fusion Estimation Method for Multi-UAV Geosynchronous Target Perception
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper presents a study of the error model based on image perception and target positioning. The interactive multi-model unscented Kalman filter algorithm for single-UAV target perception and the federated filter algorithm for multi-UAV fusion are used to achieve multi-UAV positioning fusion. Considering the effective performance of the filtering algorithm, the adaptive motion model and fusion feedback factors are established. The effectiveness of the algorithm is verified by experimental results.

articleTitle: Sequential Global Linear Programming Algorithm for Continuous Piecewise Linear Programming
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper works on a descent algorithm for continuous piecewise linear (CPWL) minimization problems. CPWL minimization is a widely applied nonlinear programming, which can be equivalently transformed into a difference of convex functions (DC) programming, and then, a concave optimization over a polyhedron. By utilizing the concavity of the objective function, the sequential global linear programming (SGLP) algorithm is proposed. The SGLP algorithm makes use of global information of the polyhedral feasible domain to gain superior optimizing capacity, while applies the mature linear programming technique to insure a rapid algorithm speed. In the numerical experiments, SGLP is compared with two other algorithms of DCA and DALPT, and shows its superior optimization efficiency.

articleTitle: Monitoring Scheme of a Ship Synchronous Generator Excitation System Based on Gaussian Process Latent Variables
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: Electricity related system has strong nonlinearity and periodicity and therefore is difficult to build data-driven models. Under the frame of Bayesian theory, Gaussian Process Latent Variable (GPLV) model is a suitable tool to model systems with such properties. With internal kernels and probabilistic features, complex data relationships can be preserved and explored. This paper attempts to construct a statistical model for a ship synchronous generator excitation system. With the proposed approach, normal load and three phase short circuit situations can be detected and differentiated successfully.

articleTitle: On the General Consensus Protocol of Third-order Multi-agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 13th World Congress on Intelligent Control and Automation (WCICA)
abstract: This paper focuses on the consensus problem of general third-order multi-agent systems. Through Laplace transform and Ruth-Hurwitz criterion, sufficient and necessary consensus conditions are obtained for continuous-time systems and discrete-time systems, respectively. Simulation results illustrate the correctness of the results.
